markdown:
# DC20Clean — Alternative Character Sheet Presentation

> Purpose: Presentation contract for the alternative character sheet at `/character2/:id`.
> Owns: Alternative-only composition, section disclosures, tab presentation, responsive layout, and alternative-only interaction choices.
> Does not own: Character state, calculations, persistence, campaign authorization, shared panel behavior, equipment rules, or PDF export.
> Authoritative source: `src/routes/character-sheet/alternative/` plus alternative-specific props passed to shared character-sheet components.
> Related systems: [Character Sheet](./CHARACTER_SHEET.MD), [Spells](./SPELLS_SYSTEM.MD), [Equipment](./EQUIPMENT_SYSTEM.MD), [Calculation](./CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD), [Campaigns](./CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD), [Testing](./TESTING_SYSTEM.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-20

## 1. Boundary

The alternative sheet is a presentation within the Character Sheet System, not a second
state-owning system. It renders under the same `CharacterSheetProvider`, reducer,
calculator output, persistence adapters, campaign read-only guards, and shared content
panels as the primary sheet.

This companion specification keeps alternative-only UI detail out of
`CHARACTER_SHEET.MD`. Shared behavior remains authoritative there.

## 2. Route and Composition

1. `/character2/:id` opens the requested saved character.
2. `/character2/` resolves the most recently modified saved character.
3. `AlternativeCharacterSheet` composes:
   1. identity and sheet actions;
   2. Resources;
   3. Attributes, Skills & Trades;
   4. Combat;
   5. Actions & Details.
4. The four main sections start expanded and collapse independently without unmounting
   their content.
5. Actions & Details reuses the shared Attacks, Spells, Inventory, Maneuvers, Features,
   Conditions, and Notes panels. The alternative tab supplies the section heading, so
   shared panels suppress duplicate top-level titles.
6. Authenticated cloud users who belong to a campaign receive the same bell, unread
   count, and campaign-feed drawer as the primary sheet.

## 3. Responsive Contract

1. Use the repository breakpoints at 768px and 1200px.
2. Prefer intrinsic grids and wrapping inside the page sections.
3. The Actions & Details tab row may scroll horizontally on narrow screens; the page
   itself must not overflow horizontally.
4. Resource cards fill the row equally and align their progress bars.
5. Exhaustion is managed as a compact resource row below the card grid.
6. Attack and inventory tables reflow inside narrow tab containers instead of relying
   on viewport width alone.

## 4. Alternative Attack Add Flow

1. `Add Weapon` opens `WeaponPickerModal`; it does not create a blank attack row.
2. The picker starts on Inventory and lists standard catalog weapons present in the
   character inventory.
3. The Inventory / Full list switch replaces the table-level catalog checkbox.
4. Full list contains the complete standard weapon catalog in alphabetical order.
5. Selecting a weapon renders the same `WeaponAttackDetails` card used by the attack
   information popup, including damage tiers, properties, features, styles,
   enhancements, conditions, and recovery rules.
6. Confirming creates one fully populated `AttackData` record and closes the picker.
7. Cancelling or closing creates no record.
8. The desktop picker uses a list/detail split. Compact layouts stack list, detail, and
   controls without horizontal page overflow.
9. Read-only campaign views do not render `Add Weapon` and therefore cannot open the
   picker.
10. Search matches weapon names, and the type filter narrows the active source to Melee
    or Ranged weapons.
11. Switching Inventory / Full list preserves the current search and type filter.
12. `Create custom weapon` is a separate action beside the source switch. It opens a
    five-panel accordion build sheet numbered Type (1), Style (2), Damage type (2.5),
    Properties (3), and Review (4). The separate damage panel keeps that choice visible
    after the complete style catalog. Its three physical damage options share one row on
    desktop and stack vertically on compact layouts.
    The Reskinning Weapons rule permits any style on either weapon type, and completed
    sections remain reopenable without losing selections. Each section shows its guidance
    beside the heading only while active, keeping the option area focused.
13. The custom builder identifies ranged Ammo and Two-Handed as automatic properties,
    exposes the Two-Handed removal cost, enforces requirements and exclusions, and uses
    the shared live weapon preview. Its sheet and preview stack on compact layouts.
14. Cancelling custom creation returns to the picker with its source, search, and filter
    unchanged. Confirmation embeds a canonical `CustomWeapon` snapshot in the new attack;
    it does not create an Equipage record, inventory row, or equipped-item effect.

Phase boundary: existing saved Equipage weapons are not selectable in this picker. The
separate builder creates a new character-local snapshot instead of depending on separate
browser-local Equipage storage.

## 5. Alternative Spell Add Flow

1. `Add Spell` opens `SpellPickerModal`; it does not create a blank spell row.
2. The picker starts on Allowed spells. This list applies the restriction of the next
   available `spellsKnownSlots` entry through `matchesSpellSlot`, including the
   Global Magic Profile when that slot is global.
3. All spells lists the complete current catalog in alphabetical order.
4. Both lists exclude spells already recorded on the character.
5. The list identifies school, cost, and sustained spells. The detail card presents
   sources, school, tags, sustained state, cost, range, duration, effects, passive text,
   and enhancements before confirmation.
6. Confirming creates one fully populated `SpellData` record and closes the picker.
7. Cancelling or closing creates no record.
8. The picker uses the weapon picker's responsive list/detail structure.
9. Read-only campaign views do not render `Add Spell`.
10. The tab uses one compact catalog toolbar: Spellbook reference, School filter,
    neutral grouped Expand/Collapse controls, and a primary Add Spell action. Controls
    wrap without changing their order when space is constrained.
11. Search matches spell names, and the picker filter narrows the active source by
    school.
12. Switching Allowed spells / All spells preserves the current search and school filter.

Phase boundary: custom-spell creation is not part of this picker. The primary sheet
retains its existing blank-row and custom-spell workflow.

### 5.1 Alternative Spell Cast Flow

1. A known spell's `Cast` action opens a focused modal for that spell. The modal does
   not duplicate the known-spell list or allow changing the selected spell.
2. The modal starts with the spell's base AP/MP cost and no enhancements declared.
3. Fixed, repeatable, variable, alternative-cost, and prerequisite-dependent spell
   enhancements use the structured saved spell data. Older rows that lack an enhancement
   snapshot resolve it through the same current-catalog lookup used by the expanded spell
   details. Repeatable and variable costs use quantity controls; alternative costs expose
   a resource-cost choice.
4. Mana Spend Limit applies to base MP plus declared enhancement MP. AP costs remain
   visible but are not automatically deducted by this Mana-only flow.
5. MP increment controls stop at both the calculated Mana Spend Limit and current Mana.
   A base cost that already exceeds either constraint disables confirmation and explains
   the failure.
6. Confirming subtracts the total MP from the shared current Mana resource, emits the
   existing spell-cast campaign event, and closes the modal. Cancelling, closing, or
   pressing Escape changes no resource.
7. Enhancement declarations are session-only casting choices; they do not rewrite the
   saved spell row.
8. This modal is alternative-only. The primary sheet retains its direct Cast behavior.

## 6. Alternative Maneuver Add Flow

1. `Add Maneuver` opens `ManeuverPickerModal`; it does not create a blank row.
2. The picker lists the current maneuver catalog alphabetically and excludes maneuvers
   already recorded on the character.
3. Each list choice identifies maneuver type and base AP/SP cost.
4. The selected card presents type, cost, range, action/reaction timing, description,
   reaction trigger when present, and every enhancement before confirmation.
5. Confirming creates one fully populated `ManeuverData` record and closes the picker.
6. Cancelling or closing creates no record.
7. The picker uses the same responsive list/detail structure as the weapon and spell pickers.
8. Read-only campaign views do not render `Add Maneuver`.
9. Search matches maneuver names, and the type filter narrows the catalog by maneuver
   type.

Phase boundary: custom-maneuver creation is not part of this picker. Maneuver
eligibility is a count budget rather than a catalog restriction, so the picker does not
present an Allowed / All source switch.

## 7. Alternative Inventory Add Flow

1. `Add Item` opens `InventoryPickerModal`; it does not create a blank inventory row.
2. Catalog lists standard inventory items alphabetically. Custom items lists saved
   Equipage records, including non-mechanical General Equipment, plus a freeform
   custom-item choice.
3. Search matches names in the active source. Catalog filters by item type; Custom items
   filters saved Equipage by equipment category.
4. Standard items preview their current rules. Saved Equipage items preview their
   stored description and properties. The freeform choice exposes name, description,
   and cost fields.
5. Quantity defaults to one and Equipped defaults to off. Both are set before
   confirmation.
6. Confirming creates one complete `InventoryItemData` record and closes the picker.
7. Cancelling or closing creates no record.
8. The picker follows the shared responsive list/detail contract and does not overflow
   the page on compact layouts.
9. Read-only campaign views do not render `Add Item`.
10. Existing inventory rows retain their explicit edit lifecycle.
11. Switching Catalog / Custom items preserves the current search and category filter.
    Filter controls remain stable across both sources, even when the active source has
    no matches for the retained category.

`CatalogPickerModal` owns the shared modal frame, accessibility behavior, search and
filter controls, list/detail layout, footer actions, Escape handling, and responsive
stacking for weapon, spell, maneuver, and inventory pickers. Each picker continues to
own its catalog eligibility, filter categories, preview content, source switches, and
record construction. Any picker with multiple sources preserves search and filter state
when the source changes.

`EquipmentBuildSheet` owns the reusable accordion structure, accessible section state,
and compact summary behavior for equipment builders. The custom-weapon builder currently
uses it; other equipment categories retain their existing Equipage builders.

## 8. Other Alternative-Only Interaction Rules

1. Attributes and combat values use the shared automatic Dice Roller.
2. The combat action panel aligns Save DC, Initiative, and Jump as equal metrics, then
   renders Walk and each calculator-returned movement mode in canonical order: Climb,
   Swim, Fly, Burrow, and Glide. Duplicate movement grants produce one display entry.
3. PD and AD use compact horizontal rows. Hit is the dominant baseline; Heavy `+5` and
   Brutal `+10` use progressively smaller values with warning and danger accents.
4. PD and AD abbreviations expose formula tooltips with live values and source bonuses.
5. PDR, EDR, and MDR share a compact footer beneath both defense rows.
6. `CharacterSheetProvider` owns the alternative sheet's normalized presentation facts.
   The Mana card and Combat Mastery consume the same provider-owned Mana visibility fact,
   which is true only when calculated maximum Mana is greater than zero. Its info control
   opens the shared MSL explanation. The provider resolves Meta Magic by canonical feature
   ID, including multiclass grants; eligible characters receive the exemption chip and
   feature-specific exception text.
7. Feature categories preserve their independent disclosure state across tab changes.
8. Existing attack, spell, inventory, maneuver, and note rows retain the explicit
   pencil / confirm / delete lifecycle. The four catalog pickers change only creation of
   new rows.
9. Upgrade-required legacy characters expose only the existing resource counters and
   Exhaustion. All Actions & Details mutation controls remain hidden.
10. Spells and Maneuvers are contextual tabs driven by the same provider-owned
    presentation facts. Spells appears only when the calculator grants at least one spell
    slot or the saved character already contains a spell. Maneuvers follows the same rule
    using the calculated maneuver budget or an existing saved maneuver. This preserves
    valid AP-only spell access and saved selections without exposing irrelevant empty panels.
11. Characters with the canonical Rage feature, including multiclass grants, receive a
    compact Rage row at the top of Combat. The row keeps cost and duration inline where
    space permits, uses one `Inactive / Active` state button, and discloses the complete
    base Rage effects plus its early-ending rule.
12. Active Rage uses the shared sheet toggle and calculator condition
    `while_raging`. The calculator applies the PD penalty, attack presentation adds
    damage only to Unarmed Strikes and melee weapons, and alternative-sheet Might Save
    rolls add one ADV stack. The roll label and Might card identify the source as
    `ADV (Rage)`; existing condition disadvantage stacks still cancel normally.
13. Automatic rolls snapshot the requested dice, mode, label, and modifier before the
    roll animation. Campaign events and toasts show the dice, signed modifier, and final
    total from that same snapshot.
14. Long Rest uses the shared sheet reset and restores HP, MP, SP, Rest Points, and Grit
    Points to maximum, clears temporary HP and Exhaustion, and emits the existing event.

## 9. Verification

1. `src/routes/character-sheet/components/Attacks.test.tsx` proves the picker creates a
   populated catalog attack and a character-local custom attack, folds in source
   switching, and sorts the catalog.
2. `src/routes/character-sheet/components/AttackPopup.test.tsx` proves the shared weapon
   detail card resolves current weapon rules.
3. `e2e/20-alternative-weapon-picker.e2e.spec.ts` proves the alternative-sheet flow and
   desktop/mobile reflow.
4. Campaign read-only behavior is covered by the lifecycle contract and Convex tests
   documented in `CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD`.
5. `AlternativeCombatResourceSection.test.tsx` proves the two-state Rage control and
   complete disclosed rule text.
6. `Maneuvers.test.tsx` proves the alternative picker creates a complete catalog-backed row, excludes existing choices, and never creates a blank row.
7. `AlternativeMasterySection.test.tsx` and
   `alternativeRollPresentation.test.ts` prove the visible Rage source and ADV/DisADV
   stack cancellation.
8. The deferred character-level magic, feature-mode, and derived-calculation suite is
   specified in `TESTING_SYSTEM.MD` section 3.3.
9. `src/routes/character-sheet/components/Spells.test.tsx` proves the alternative
   picker opens without mutation, applies next-slot restrictions, switches to an
   alphabetical full catalog, and confirms one populated spell.
10. `Attacks.test.tsx`, `Spells.test.tsx`, and `Maneuvers.test.tsx` prove picker search
    and domain filters narrow their active catalogs. Weapon and spell coverage also
    proves that source changes preserve the current search and filter.
11. `Inventory.test.tsx` proves the alternative picker opens without mutation, searches
    and filters the catalog, preserves search and category state across source changes,
    applies quantity and equipped state, and confirms one complete inventory row.
12. `e2e/21-alternative-inventory-picker.e2e.spec.ts` proves the inventory picker flow,
    populated-row creation, responsive reflow, and horizontal-overflow guard.
13. `spellCastSpend.test.ts` proves fixed, repeatable, variable, alternative-cost, and
    prerequisite calculations. `Spells.test.tsx` proves the focused modal, MSL guard,
    Mana deduction, campaign callback, and close-on-confirm behavior.
14. `e2e/22-alternative-spell-cast.e2e.spec.ts` proves the current-rules alternative
    sheet opens the modal, stops enhancement MP at MSL, confirms the cast, and visibly
    reduces the Mana card.
15. `CampaignFeedAction.test.tsx` proves the shared bell marks notifications seen and
    opens the feed without mounting cloud hooks when cloud authentication is unavailable.
16. `DiceRoller.test.tsx`, `campaignEventFormat.test.ts`, and `longRest.test.ts` prove
    automatic-roll totals, party-event formatting, and complete Long Rest restoration.
17. `e2e/23-alternative-long-rest.e2e.spec.ts` proves the alternative-sheet action
    visibly restores spent Grit and persists the restored value across reload.

markdown:
# Analytics System

> Purpose: Define product-analytics collection, identity, privacy boundaries, event contracts, reporting semantics, and operational setup.
> Owns: PostHog client initialization, explicit pageview capture, acquisition attribution, authenticated identity, analytics event registration, privacy filtering, and analytics verification.
> Does not own: Application logs, error reporting, source user records, authorization, access-policy enforcement, legal determinations, final privacy-notice text, PostHog billing, or retention settings.
> Authoritative source: `src/lib/analytics/`, `src/components/analytics/PostHogLifecycle.tsx`, `src/components/auth/CurrentUserContext.tsx`, `convex/users.ts`, and analytics environment variables.
> Related systems: `PRIVACY_AND_LEGAL_SYSTEM.MD`, `DATABASE_SYSTEM.MD`, `CHARACTER_CREATION_FLOW.MD`, `PROJECT_TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.MD`, `TESTING_SYSTEM.MD`.
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-21

## 1. Goals and Boundaries

1. The system answers five initial questions:
   1. How many people use the application?
   2. Which routes and major features do they use?
   3. Where did visits originate?
   4. How many visitors progress from a pageview through sign-in to character creation?
   5. When were identified accounts created?
2. The system deliberately does not provide:
   1. Session replay.
   2. Click or form autocapture.
   3. User-authored content analysis.
   4. Error or performance monitoring; Sentry remains the intended error-reporting boundary.
   5. Authorization decisions. Analytics data must never decide who can use a feature.

## 2. Provider and Control Plane

1. Product analytics uses PostHog Cloud EU.
2. Operational identifiers:
   1. Organization: `DC20Clean`.
   2. Project ID: `278381`.
   3. Ingestion host: `https://eu.i.posthog.com`.
   4. Authorized production URL: `https://dc20clean.vercel.app`.
3. The PostHog project token is a public, write-only browser token. It belongs in deployment configuration but must not be copied into documentation.
4. Production configuration is stored in Vercel. Analytics and the draft legal/consent flow have independent flags. Development and preview remain disabled unless a deliberate validation run supplies the variables. Neither flag constitutes legal approval.
5. Vercel Analytics is not part of the runtime. Do not run both providers without an explicit migration decision.

## 3. Runtime Architecture

The two event paths are:

```text
route or auth change
  -> PostHogLifecycle
  -> resolve anonymous or Convex identity
  -> build minimal pageview properties
  -> privacy sanitizer
  -> PostHog EU

registered product action
  -> logger.track
  -> event/property/value allowlist
  -> privacy sanitizer
  -> PostHog EU
```

1. `PostHogLifecycle` is mounted inside `BrowserRouter` and under the application auth providers.
2. The PostHog SDK is dynamically imported when analytics is enabled and a pageview or registered event needs capture. If the legal/consent flow is enabled, it additionally waits for a valid affirmative choice; a missing, refused, expired, or revision-stale choice keeps the SDK unloaded. With that flow disabled, no in-app choice is required. The SDK does not add to the initial application bundle when analytics is disabled.
3. Convex mode waits for both auth and `users.getCurrentUser` to resolve before the first pageview. This prevents an authenticated visit from first being recorded as anonymous and then split incorrectly.
4. Local-storage-only mode has no Convex identity and captures anonymous pageviews immediately.
5. Route changes are deduplicated by `pathname + search`. Hash-only changes are not separate pageviews.
6. The SDK is a singleton. React Strict Mode rerenders do not create duplicate pageviews because the lifecycle keeps the previous route and identity in refs.

## 4. Environment Contract

```dotenv
VITE_ENABLE_ANALYTICS=true
VITE_ENABLE_LEGAL_CONSENT_FLOW=false
VITE_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN=phc_...
VITE_POSTHOG_HOST=https://eu.i.posthog.com
```

1. Analytics loads when `VITE_ENABLE_ANALYTICS=true` and a non-empty project token is present. If `VITE_ENABLE_LEGAL_CONSENT_FLOW=true`, it additionally requires a valid affirmative choice. When that flag is false, collection proceeds without an in-app consent choice.
2. `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST` defaults to the EU ingestion host.
3. All four values are browser-visible Vite configuration. None grants read or administrative access to PostHog.
4. To disable collection, set `VITE_ENABLE_ANALYTICS=false` and redeploy the frontend. Changing the legal/consent flag is not an analytics kill switch.

## 5. Identity Lifecycle

| Application state                                            | PostHog action                            | Result                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Auth is unresolved                                           | None                                      | No event is sent until ownership is known.                           |
| Anonymous visitor                                            | Keep PostHog anonymous ID                 | Pageviews remain anonymous.                                          |
| User resolves as authenticated                               | `identify(Convex userId)`                 | Anonymous history is merged into the stable account identity.        |
| Different authenticated user replaces a persisted user       | `reset()`, then `identify(new userId)`    | Events from different accounts do not share one browser identity.    |
| Live authenticated user signs out                            | Capture `user_signed_out`, then `reset()` | Subsequent events use a fresh anonymous ID.                          |
| Signed-out load finds a stale authenticated PostHog identity | `reset()`                                 | The stale identity is cleared without claiming an observed sign-out. |

1. The only distinct ID supplied by the application is the stable Convex `userId`.
2. Email and display name are not sent to PostHog.
3. `users.getCurrentUser` returns `userId`, optional display name for application UI, and the Convex user document `_creationTime` as `createdAt`.
4. The lifecycle sends only `createdAt`, converted to ISO format as the `account_created_at` person property.
5. Invalid timestamps are ignored instead of breaking identity or pageview capture.
6. `undefined` means the current-user query is unresolved; `null` means it resolved without an authenticated user. Consumers must preserve this distinction.

## 6. Pageviews and Acquisition

1. Pageviews are captured explicitly after identity reconciliation.
2. The application supplies a minimal pageview envelope:
   1. Sanitized `$current_url` without query or hash.
   2. Sanitized `$pathname`.
   3. `$host`.
   4. Referrer origin and referring domain, or `$direct`.
   5. Valid `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, and `utm_campaign` values from the entry URL.
3. PostHog's automatic campaign and referrer persistence is disabled. This prevents raw URLs, query strings, referrer paths, and click identifiers from being stored in the SDK's local persistence.
4. Acquisition values must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, begin with an alphanumeric character, and be at most 64 characters. Invalid values are dropped.
5. `utm_content`, `utm_term`, search keywords, and advertising click identifiers are dropped. They are not needed for the initial reporting questions and can contain personal or high-cardinality data.
6. Referrers are reduced to their origin. The referring domain remains available for source reporting; external path and query data do not.

### 6.1 Dynamic route normalization

| Runtime path                                    | Analytics path                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `/character/:id`                                | `/character/:id`                                |
| `/character/:id/edit`                           | `/character/:id/edit`                           |
| `/character/:id/levelup`                        | `/character/:id/levelup`                        |
| `/character2/:id`                               | `/character2/:id`                               |
| `/dm/monsters/:id`                              | `/dm/monsters/:id`                              |
| `/dm/encounters/:id`                            | `/dm/encounters/:id`                            |
| `/campaigns/join/:code`                         | `/campaigns/join/:code`                         |
| `/campaigns/:id`                                | `/campaigns/:id`                                |
| `/campaigns/:campaignId/character/:characterId` | `/campaigns/:campaignId/character/:characterId` |

1. The sanitizer applies to current, initial, session-entry, and previous-pageview URL/path properties. Only known static routes pass unchanged; rulebook subroutes reduce to `/rulebook/*`, and every unrecognized path reduces to `/other`. URL credentials, queries, and hashes are removed.
2. Every new route must be reviewed and added to the static allowlist or `PRIVATE_ROUTE_PATTERNS` with a focused test before it appears as a separate analytics path.

## 7. Custom Event Registry

`src/lib/analytics/posthog.ts` is the executable event contract. Unregistered events and properties are dropped.

| Event                           | Emission owner                                   | Allowed properties and values                                                     | Meaning                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sign_in_started`               | `SignIn` before Google auth starts               | `provider=google`; `feature=general\|cloud-save\|pdf-export`                      | A visitor initiated authentication.                                                                                |
| `sign_in_failed`                | `SignIn` when auth initiation throws             | Same as `sign_in_started`                                                         | Authentication failed before redirect or local completion. OAuth callback failures after redirect are not covered. |
| `authenticated_session_started` | Identity lifecycle                               | None                                                                              | An authenticated account resolved for this application load or identity transition.                                |
| `user_signed_out`               | Identity lifecycle                               | None                                                                              | A live authenticated identity became signed out before reset.                                                      |
| `character_creation_completed`  | `completeCharacter` after successful persistence | `class_id` and `ancestry_id`: safe IDs up to 64 characters; `level`: integer 1–20 | A new character was persisted successfully. Non-persisting builds used by level-up do not emit it.                 |

1. Allowed event values are validated, not merely property names.
2. Character names, player names, character record IDs, error text, notes, campaign names, and other free text are forbidden.
3. `logger.track` is a compatibility entry point. New callers still require an explicit registry change and tests.

## 8. Privacy Configuration

1. The SDK configuration explicitly disables:
   1. Autocapture.
   2. Automatic pageviews and page-leave events.
   3. Session recording.
   4. Exception and performance capture.
   5. Heatmaps and dead-click capture.
   6. Surveys, product tours, conversations, and external extension loading.
   7. Feature flags, remote decide calls, toolbar metrics, browser console-log capture, and network metrics.
   8. Automatic campaign and referrer persistence.
2. Additional constraints:
   1. Person profiles are created only for identified users.
   2. IP-based enrichment is disabled.
   3. Browser Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals are respected.
   4. Persistence is localStorage-only and cross-subdomain cookies are disabled.
   5. URL hashes are disabled at the SDK level and removed again by the privacy sanitizer.
   6. PostHog's personal-data masking remains enabled as defense in depth.
3. Standard non-content technical metadata may still accompany events: browser, browser version, operating system, device type, viewport/screen dimensions, language, SDK version, session ID, anonymous device/distinct ID, and event timestamp.
4. The application must never send saved game data or user-authored text.
5. Respecting Do Not Track does not replace the publication review below.

### 8.1 Publication review and flag behavior

The two deployment modes are intentional and must be reviewed independently:

1. `VITE_ENABLE_LEGAL_CONSENT_FLOW=false`: no consent dialog or preference control; `/privacy` and `/terms` redirect to `/menu`; their footer and sign-in links are absent. If analytics is enabled, PostHog starts without an in-app choice, including for a browser that previously refused analytics. This mode does **not** establish that collection is consent-exempt or legally approved. It also leaves no app-hosted privacy notice for visitors. Do not silently treat this switch as a privacy approval.
2. `VITE_ENABLE_LEGAL_CONSENT_FLOW=true`: the draft legal routes and links are visible. `ConsentManager` supplies a one-optional-category choice, stores a versioned choice for 182 days, and provides a footer preference control. The lifecycle and SDK adapter fail closed until the choice is valid. Withdrawal stops future capture and clears local PostHog identity, but cannot erase events already sent.

Before a production decision, the operator must resolve and document the applicable notice/consent basis, public disclosure, PostHog DPA, actual retention and deletion process, intended user ages, and contact/data-request path. The draft notices still contain unresolved facts and are not approved for publication. Set a product target of at most 13 months for identifiable raw analytics events, and verify provider enforcement or a deletion process. Browser verification must cover the selected mode, sign-in/out, Do Not Track, the event allowlist, and the independent feedback boundary. If enabling the consent mode, also test first visit, refusal, acceptance, return visit, withdrawal, expiry, and revision changes.

The existing privacy controls—EU hosting, project-level client-IP discard, event allowlists, route sanitization, and disabled replay/autocapture—remain required but do not resolve these decisions. Identifying visitors with a stable Convex user ID and storing a PostHog identifier in localStorage must not be described as anonymous audience measurement. PostHog's [GDPR guidance](https://posthog.com/docs/privacy/gdpr-compliance) recommends explicit consent for product analytics; [CNIL's audience-measurement exception](https://www.cnil.fr/en/sheet-ndeg16-use-analytics-your-websites-and-applications) has narrower conditions, including no cross-checking with customer records.

## 9. Reporting Contract

### 9.1 Built-in web analytics

Use the PostHog Web Analytics dashboard for:

1. Unique visitors, pageviews, and route usage.
2. Referring domains and safe UTM source/medium/campaign values.
3. Device and browser breakdowns.
4. Active hours and basic retention from pageview events.

Do not treat bounce rate, scroll depth, or exact session duration as authoritative. Those metrics depend on page-leave or autocapture signals intentionally disabled by this system.

### 9.2 Product insights

1. Acquisition: unique `$pageview` visitors by `$referring_domain`, `utm_source`, and `utm_medium`.
2. Activation funnel: `$pageview` → `sign_in_started` → `authenticated_session_started` → `character_creation_completed`.
3. Authenticated active users: unique identified users emitting `authenticated_session_started`, viewed daily, weekly, and monthly.
4. Feature usage: unique visitors by sanitized `$pathname`.
5. Signup history: identified people grouped by `account_created_at`.

### 9.3 Interpretation limits

1. Collection begins only after a deployment containing this system. Historical visits and acquisition sources cannot be reconstructed.
2. Existing accounts receive their real Convex creation timestamp when they next authenticate.
3. Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control, ad blockers, network failures, and disabled environments cause undercounting.
4. Referrer and UTM attribution is directional, not a complete causal account of how someone discovered the application.
5. Direct traffic can include visits whose referrer was unavailable.

## 10. Change Procedure

### 10.1 Add a custom event

1. Define the product question the event answers. Do not add events speculatively.
2. Add the event and the smallest property allowlist to `EVENT_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST`.
3. Add strict value validation in `sanitizeEventProperty`.
4. Emit only after the user-visible action succeeds.
5. Add unit coverage proving allowed values pass and private/unregistered values are dropped.
6. Update the registry and reporting section in this document.

### 10.2 Add or change a route

1. Determine whether any path segment can contain an ID, join code, name, or user-controlled value.
2. Add a safe static route to `PUBLIC_ROUTES`, or a dynamic pattern to `PRIVATE_ROUTE_PATTERNS`, before the route ships if it needs its own analytics label. Otherwise it is grouped under `/other`.
3. Test current, initial, session-entry, and previous-pageview path normalization.
4. Confirm query strings and hashes remain absent from ingested events.

### 10.3 Change identity

1. Keep the Convex user ID as the sole stable distinct ID.
2. Never switch to email, display name, character ID, or device-specific application IDs.
3. Preserve identify-before-pageview and reset-before-anonymous-pageview ordering.
4. Add lifecycle tests for every new identity transition.

## 11. Verification and Operations

### 11.1 Automated verification

1. Privacy unit tests cover:
   1. Every dynamic route.
   2. Query/hash removal.
   3. Referrer-origin reduction.
   4. Campaign-value constraints.
   5. Search term and click-ID removal.
2. Client tests cover:
   1. Waiting for auth resolution.
   2. Initial identification and pageview context.
   3. Strict Mode/rerender deduplication.
   4. Logout identity handoff.
3. Analytics-client tests cover:
   1. Privacy configuration.
   2. Identity-before-pageview ordering.
   3. Reset-on-logout ordering.
   4. Event/property/value allowlisting.
   5. The SDK adapter runs in the server test project because its environment setup is process-backed; privacy and React lifecycle tests also run in the browser project.
4. Convex tests cover unauthenticated and authenticated `users.getCurrentUser` responses.
5. Character-completion tests prove only a successfully persisted new character emits `character_creation_completed`.

### 11.2 Production verification

After every analytics rollout:

1. Confirm the deployment's analytics token, host, enable flag, and independently chosen legal/consent flag. Verify that the operator resolved the publication review in Section 8.1 before collection.
2. Open a public route and verify one `$pageview` reaches project `278381`.
3. Open a dynamic route and verify no runtime ID, query string, or hash appears in the event.
4. Follow a safe UTM link and verify only source, medium, and campaign are present.
5. Authenticate and verify:
   1. The distinct ID is the Convex user ID.
   2. `account_created_at` is present.
   3. Email and display name are absent.
6. Sign out and verify the next pageview has a new anonymous identity.
7. Complete a new character and verify the registered event contains only its allowed properties.
8. Confirm no session recordings, autocapture events, exceptions, browser logs, or network metrics are arriving.

### 11.3 Failure behavior

1. SDK import or initialization failure is silent and must not block application behavior.
2. Analytics capture is fire-and-forget. Product actions never await PostHog delivery.
3. Invalid routes, attribution values, timestamps, events, or properties are dropped rather than sent unsafely.
4. If unexpected private data appears, disable analytics in Vercel, redeploy, then correct the sanitizer before re-enabling it.

# DC20Clean – Ancestry System > Purpose: Reference for ancestry data, ancestry trait pools, ancestry-point selection, and ancestry creation UI. > Owns: Ancestry definitions, ancestry composition, ancestry selection, ancestry-point spending, and ancestry-facing trait availability. > Does not own: Trait mechanics, generic effect semantics, derived-stat formulas, or the overall character-creation sequence. > Authoritative source: `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md`, `docs/migration/ancestries-v0105-report.json`, and `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/ancestries.ts`. > Related systems: [Traits](./TRAITS_SYSTEM.MD), [Effects](./EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD), [Calculation](./CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD), [Character Creation](./CHARACTER_CREATION_FLOW.MD). > Status: Active > Last Updated: 2026-07-21 --- ## 1 High-Level Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Rule-Data A1[ancestries/traits.ts] A2[ancestries/ancestries.ts] style A1 fill:#4ade80,color:#000 style A2 fill:#4ade80,color:#000 end subgraph Types & Schemas B1[schemas/types.ts – ITrait / IAncestry] B2[schemas/character.schema.ts – Zod Effects] end A1 --> B1 A2 --> B1 subgraph Compile-Time Validation C1[rulesdata.spec.ts] end A1 --> C1 A2 --> C1 B2 --> C1 subgraph Runtime D1[enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts] D2[React Context + useCharacterBuilder] D3[UI Components
SelectedAncestries.tsx
AncestrySelector.tsx
CharacterSheetProvider.tsx] end A1 & A2 --> D1 --> D2 --> D3 ``` --- ## 2 Key Files & Their Roles | Layer | File / Dir | Responsibility | | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Rule Data (canonical)** | `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/traits.ts` | Declarative list of `traitsData` objects | | | `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/ancestries.ts` | Declarative list of core `ancestriesData` (11 ancestries) | | | `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/sharedTraits.ts` | Shared trait definitions used across ancestries | | | `scripts/ancestries/dc20-0105-ancestries.mjs` | Source parser/audit generator for the v0.10.5 ancestry chapter | | | `docs/migration/ancestries-v0105-report.json` | Generated source audit report used by tests to detect runtime drift | | **Type Contracts** | `src/lib/rulesdata/schemas/types.ts` | TS interfaces `ITrait`, `IAncestry`, `ITraitEffect` | | | `src/lib/rulesdata/schemas/character.schema.ts` | Zod schema used for validation & effect typing | | **Validation Tests** | `src/lib/rulesdata/rulesdata.spec.ts` | Loads every trait / ancestry and asserts schema compliance | | **Runtime Engine** | `src/lib/services/enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts` | Aggregates effects, resolves choices, outputs stats | | **State Layer** | `src/lib/stores/characterContext.tsx`
`src/lib/hooks/useCharacterBuilder.ts` | Provides calculated results to UI | | **UI** | `src/routes/character-creation/*` (selection)
`src/routes/character-sheet/*` (display) | Import `ancestriesData` / `traitsData` directly | Note: Class features can modify ancestry budgets via effects (e.g., Cleric “Ancestral” domain adds `+2` to `ancestryPoints`). Ensure such effects are applied before spending ancestry points. --- ## Ancestry and Trait Subsystem Boundary The implementation and docs model ancestry and traits as two related subsystems: - **Ancestry subsystem**: owns ancestry records, core/non-core ancestry availability, default and expanded trait pools, ancestry-point budgets, variant trait set references, and the character-creation selection flow. - **Trait subsystem**: owns the reusable trait catalog, trait costs, prerequisites, effect definitions, effect confidence/automation classification, and calculator/sheet effect integration. Current boundary: - Keep `docs/systems/ANCESTRY_SYSTEM.MD` focused on ancestry selection and trait-pool composition. - Keep `docs/systems/TRAITS_SYSTEM.MD` focused on individual trait data and effects. - Move duplicated trait checklist/testing details out of this doc and into `TRAITS_SYSTEM.MD`. - Keep the generated v0.10.5 ancestry audit script/report able to validate both layers, but have tests assert ancestry concerns and trait concerns in separate describe blocks or separate files. - Ancestry data stays in `ancestries/ancestries.ts`; the trait catalog remains in `ancestries/traits.ts` as the trait subsystem boundary. - `traits.contract.test.ts` owns the focused trait-record and structured-reference contract. The broader ancestry audit continues validating cross-layer composition. This boundary intentionally changes no runtime behavior or storage shape. --- ## 3 Adding **New Ancestry** – Checklist ✅ 1. **Data** 1.1 Append the ancestry object to `ancestries/ancestries.ts` ‑ `id`, `name`, `description`, `defaultTraitIds`, `expandedTraitIds`. ‑ `rulesSource` (string, e.g., `DC20Beta0.95`). 2. **Traits** 2.1 Create each new trait in `ancestries/traits.ts` ‑ Use unique `id = '_'`. ‑ Ensure `cost`, `description`, and `effects` array. 2.2 ⚠️ **Human-in-the-loop review required**: First attempt to reuse existing `effect.type` strings. If a new type seems unavoidable, a maintainer must review and approve the required engine & schema changes (see §4). 3. **Types / Schema** 3.1 If a new `effect.type` is invented, add to Zod schema in `character.schema.ts` **and** implement logic in `enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts`. 4. **Calculator Support** 4.1 If the effect is **numeric** → map in `createStatBreakdown` or similar. 4.2 If it’s an **ability** → emit as `GRANT_ABILITY` (requires no engine change). 5. **UI** 5.1 No code changes: components import arrays directly. 5.2 Edge-cases: add banner images / icons if needed. 6. **Tests** 6.1 Run `npm run test:unit`; `rulesdata.spec.ts` will fail on schema violations. 6.2 Add a specific calculation test if the trait is complex. 7. **Docs** 7.1 Append a bullet to this file under “Next Ancestries Added”. 8. **Commit Message Template** ``` feat(rules): add ancestry & N traits - traits.ts: +N entries - ancestries.ts: +1 entry - tests: update counts ``` --- ## 4 Adding **New Trait Effect Type** – Decision Matrix | Question | Yes | No | | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | | Does an existing `effect.type` cover the mechanic? | Use it → go to Step 3.1 | Create new type → continue | | Does the effect alter a **numeric stat**? | Implement in calculator (`createStatBreakdown`) | Use `GRANT_ABILITY` + manual rules text | | Does the UI need to resolve **user choice**? | Add `userChoiceRequired` in trait & update `resolveEffectChoices` | — | **When new type is created**: 1. Extend `ITraitEffect.type` JSDoc comment (open list). 2. Extend Zod schema validation. 3. Implement logic in calculator. 4. Write unit test(s). --- ## 5 Troubleshooting FAQ 🤖 | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | | **Vite import error** for traits/ancestries | File path typo (should be `ancestries/...`) | Search `import .*rulesdata/traits` etc. | | New ancestry not visible in UI | Not added to `ancestries/ancestries.ts` or wrong `id` | Check default/expanded trait IDs | | Unit test `rulesdata.spec.ts` fails | Schema violation (missing field / wrong effect) | Inspect test output & update data | | Stats not updating for new effect | Effect type not handled in calculator | Add case to `createStatBreakdown` | --- ## 6 Testing 🧪 ### 6.1 Test Suite **Location**: `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/ancestries.test.ts` **Coverage**: 48 comprehensive tests validating: #### Data Structure & Schema Compliance - ✅ Ancestry data loads successfully - ✅ All required fields present (`id`, `name`, `description`, `rulesSource`, `defaultTraitIds`, `expandedTraitIds`) - ✅ Unique ancestry IDs and names - ✅ **Non-empty trait lists** (every ancestry must have at least one trait) - ✅ Valid `rulesSource` values - ✅ Trait data loads successfully - ✅ All required trait fields present (`id`, `name`, `description`, `cost`, `effects`) - ✅ Unique trait IDs - ✅ Valid cost values (numeric) - ✅ Non-empty effects arrays #### ID Format & Naming Conventions - ✅ `ancestry_trait` naming convention followed - ✅ `snake_case` for ancestry IDs - ✅ Trait ID prefixes match ancestry IDs #### Trait-to-Ancestry Relationships - ✅ All referenced traits exist in `defaultTraitIds` - ✅ All referenced traits exist in `expandedTraitIds` - ✅ No duplicates between default and expanded - ✅ No duplicate trait IDs within lists - ✅ **Zero orphaned traits** (all traits referenced by at least one ancestry) #### Effect System Validation - ✅ Only valid effect types used - ✅ Valid target values for `MODIFY_STAT` effects - ✅ Numeric values for numeric effect types - ✅ Proper `userChoice` structure for choice-based effects - ✅ **All effects have required `target` field** #### Cost & Budget Validation - ✅ Default trait costs calculate correctly (should equal 5 for most ancestries) - ✅ Valid costs for negative traits (negative values, `isNegative: true`) - ✅ Consistent cost structure across all traits #### Schema Compliance - ✅ Valid optional fields when present - ✅ Valid effect structure for all effects #### Data Coverage Statistics - ✅ Reports total ancestry count (11) - ✅ Reports total trait count (`traitsData` has 178 core traits; source report has 180 including Fallen/Redeemed variant traits) - ✅ Reports trait distribution per ancestry - ✅ Reports effect type usage distribution - ✅ Reports cost distribution - ✅ Confirms the runtime ancestry list matches the generated v0.10.5 core source report - ✅ Confirms magazine/non-core ancestries are absent from runtime data ### 6.2 Running Tests ```bash # Run ancestry tests only npm run test:unit -- ancestries.test.ts # Run all unit tests npm run test:unit # Run with UI (useful for debugging) npm run test:unit -- ancestries.test.ts --ui ``` ### 6.3 Test-Driven Data Quality The test suite enforces strict data quality rules: - **No placeholder ancestries**: Every ancestry must have traits defined - **No orphaned traits**: Every trait must be referenced by at least one ancestry - **No missing references**: All trait IDs in ancestry lists must exist - **Strict schema**: All effects must have `type`, `target`, and `value` fields - **Naming conventions**: IDs must follow `ancestry_trait` pattern ### 6.4 When Tests Fail | Test Failure | Common Causes | Fix | | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | | "should have non-empty trait lists" | Added ancestry with empty trait arrays | Add traits or remove placeholder ancestry | | "should reference only existing traits" | Typo in trait ID, or trait not defined | Fix ID or create the missing trait | | "should not have orphaned traits" | Trait defined but not referenced by any ancestry | Add to an ancestry's trait list or remove trait | | "should have valid effect structure" | Missing `target` field in effect | Add `target` field (not `count` or `options`) | | "should follow ancestry_trait naming" | Trait ID doesn't match `ancestry_trait` pattern | Rename trait ID to match pattern | --- ## 7 Beastborn Traits The Beastborn ancestry includes a diverse set of traits representing various animal adaptations. Recent additions include: - `beastborn_web_walk` — Walk on webs and similar surfaces - `beastborn_prehensile_tail` — Use tail as an additional limb - `beastborn_camouflage` — Blend into natural environments - `beastborn_echolocation` — Navigate using sound waves - `beastborn_pack_tactics` — Gain advantage when fighting alongside allies ### 7.1 Prerequisite Patterns: `requirements.hasTrait` Some traits use the `requirements.hasTrait` pattern for "any-of" prerequisites (OR logic), which supersedes the simple `prerequisites` array. This allows a trait to require any one of multiple possible traits: ```typescript { id: 'beastborn_enhanced_flight', name: 'Enhanced Flight', prerequisites: ['beastborn_winged_arms'], // Legacy: requires this specific trait // OR requirements: { hasTrait: ['beastborn_winged_arms', 'beastborn_webbed_hands'] // Requires ANY of these traits } } ``` When `requirements.hasTrait` is present, the trait requires any ONE of the listed traits to be selected (OR logic), making it more flexible than the single-trait `prerequisites` array. ## 8 Variant Traits Some ancestries have `variantTraits` arrays containing alternative trait sets. These are not separate ancestries but optional trait replacements: - `angelborn` → `angelborn_fallen` variant - `fiendborn` → `fiendborn_redeemed` variant Variant traits follow the same schema as regular traits and are available for selection alongside default/expanded traits. --- ## 9 Future Evolution - **Effect Processor** integration will further centralise logic—update §3 Step 4 when landed. - **Schema-driven forms** may auto-render trait editors using this document's file maps. ## 10 DC20 v0.10.5 Notes - Core runtime scope is limited to the 11 core v0.10.5 ancestries: Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, Gnome, Orc, Dragonborn, Giantborn, Angelborn, Fiendborn, and Beastborn. - Magazine/non-core ancestries are not in runtime data: Gremlin, Goblin, Terraborn, Shadowborn, and Psyborn. - `npm run ancestries:generate:0105` parses `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md` and writes `docs/migration/ancestries-v0105-report.json`. - `npm run ancestries:validate:0105` re-parses the source and fails if the generated report is stale. - `ancestries.test.ts` compares every runtime core ancestry's exposed trait names and costs against the generated source report. Runtime descriptions/effects remain human-reviewed. - `Hazardous Hide` is present under the stable `beastborn_hazardous_hide` ID and source-confirmed as a returned v0.10.5 Beastborn Body trait. - `Additional Limb` and `Capable Limb` keep their stable Beastborn IDs while matching v0.10.5 wording. `Capable Limb` costs 2 points and allows Weapons, Shields, Spell Focuses, and Somatic Components once per Additional Limb. - `beastborn_natural_weapon_style` is the current v0.10.5 Beastborn Natural Weapon trait. `beastborn_natural_weapon_passive` and `beastborn_prehensile_appendage` are not core v0.10.5 traits. - No trait alias was required for this pass; saved trait IDs remain stable. --- > _Last updated: 2026-06-19_ > Maintainer: @DC20Clean-Team

# DC20Clean – Background System (Skills, Trades, Languages) > Purpose: Canonical reference for Background skills, trades, languages, point budgets, conversions, validation, and UI wiring. > Owns: Background option data, allocation budgets, conversions, mastery spending behavior, and Background-stage validation and presentation. > Does not own: Global mastery-cap policy, generic effect semantics, class progression grants, or character-creation orchestration. > Authoritative source: `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md`, `docs/migration/background-v0105-report.json`, `src/lib/rulesdata/skills.ts`, `src/lib/rulesdata/trades.ts`, `src/lib/rulesdata/languages.ts`, and the calculator Background modules. > Related systems: [Calculation](./CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD), [Effects](./EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD), [Character Creation](./CHARACTER_CREATION_FLOW.MD), [Traits](./TRAITS_SYSTEM.MD). > Status: Active > Last Updated: 2026-07-21 --- ## 1 High-Level Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Rule-Data A1[rulesdata/skills.ts] A2[rulesdata/trades.ts] A3[rulesdata/languages.ts] style A1 fill:#4ade80,color:#000 style A2 fill:#4ade80,color:#000 style A3 fill:#4ade80,color:#000 end subgraph Types & Schemas B1[schemas/types.ts – ISkillData / ITradeData / ILanguageData] B2[schemas/character.schema.ts – Effect union + Mastery Cap Effects] end A1 & A2 & A3 --> B1 subgraph Runtime D1[enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts
calculateCharacterWithBreakdowns] D2[React Context + useCharacterBuilder] D3[UI Components
Background.tsx
components/LanguagesTab.tsx
components/SkillsTab.tsx
components/TradesTab.tsx] end B1 --> D1 --> D2 --> D3 ``` --- ## 2 Key Files & Their Roles | Layer | File / Dir | Responsibility | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Rule Data (canonical) | `src/lib/rulesdata/skills.ts` | Declarative `skillsData` array | | | `src/lib/rulesdata/trades.ts` | Declarative `tradesData` array (see also `docs/archive/TRADES_MULTI_ATTRIBUTE_SPEC.md`) | | | `src/lib/rulesdata/languages.ts` | Declarative `languagesData` array | | | `scripts/background/dc20-0105-background.mjs` | Source parser/audit generator for the v0.10.5 background chapter | | | `scripts/background/dc20-0105-background-names.ts` | App-data name validator for skills, trades, and languages against the generated report | | | `scripts/background/dc20-0105-background-trait-effects.ts` | Trait impact audit for Background point pools and mastery caps | | | `docs/migration/background-v0105-report.json` | Generated source audit report for skills, trades, languages, budgets, and conversions | | | `docs/migration/background-trait-effects-v0105.json` | Generated report of ancestry trait effects that modify Background | | Type Contracts | `src/lib/rulesdata/schemas/types.ts` | `ISkillData`, `ITradeData`, `ILanguageData` | | Runtime Engine | `src/lib/services/enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts` | Computes base budgets, applies trait bonuses, conversions, and usage | | State Layer | `src/lib/stores/characterContext.tsx` | Stores background point allocations and conversion counts | | Hook | `src/lib/hooks/useCharacterBuilder.ts` | Runs calculator and returns `calculationResult.background` | | UI | `src/routes/character-creation/Background.tsx` and tabs | Renders editors for skills/trades/languages | --- ## 3 Data Shapes - Skills: `ISkillData { id, name, attributeAssociation, description }` - Trades: `ITradeData { id, name, primaryAttribute, attributeAssociations[], description, tools? }` - For multi-attribute trades, see `docs/archive/TRADES_MULTI_ATTRIBUTE_SPEC.md` (canonical field: `attributeAssociations: string[]`). - Languages: `ILanguageData { id, name, family: 'mortal'|'exotic'|'divine'|'outer', description, typicalSpeakers, checkDc, legacyIds? }` Background allocations in store: - `skillsData: Record` – mastery levels per skill - `tradesData: Record` – mastery levels per trade - `languagesData: Record` – per-language fluency - `skillMasteryLimitElevations: Record` – extra Skill Points spent to raise a specific Skill's mastery limit - `tradeMasteryLimitElevations: Record` – extra Trade Points spent to raise a specific Trade's mastery limit - Conversions: `{ skillToTrade, tradeToSkill, tradeToLanguage }` numbers on the store Persistence note: `skillMasteryLimitElevations` and `tradeMasteryLimitElevations` are written to the saved character root by `characterCompletion.ts` (always present, default `{}`). They must be declared in `convex/schema.ts` `characterValidator` — Convex strict-validates documents on insert, so any undeclared root field makes `characters.create` throw a generic `Server Error`. Both are stored as `v.optional(v.record(v.string(), v.object({ source: v.string(), value: v.number() })))`. After editing the schema, redeploy the Convex backend (`npx convex deploy`) or prod will keep rejecting new characters. Source-audit note: v0.10.5 explicitly supports `skillToTrade` and `tradeToLanguage`. `tradeToSkill` is not a legal source conversion. It is retained only as a legacy/undo field and is normalized by the calculator so it can cancel prior `skillToTrade` entries but can never create Skill Points from base Trade Points. DC20 0.10.5 language catalog notes: - Selectable languages come from the official 0.10.5 families: Mortal, Exotic, Divine, and Outer. - Limited-language checks use family DCs from the rules text: Mortal 10, Exotic 15, Divine 15, Outer 20. - Legacy save IDs are preserved where practical for unchanged entries, and renamed families may expose alias metadata (`legacyIds`) so the current picker can surface old selections without reintroducing retired names into the catalog. - Saved legacy aliases, such as `primordial`, display with the current canonical catalog name (`Elemental`) in creator, sheet, and export surfaces. - The explicit v0.10 upgrade reports both sides of consolidated languages before confirmation. When Abyssal and Infernal both convert to Fiendish, the converter keeps the strongest purchased fluency. - Unsupported legacy selections (for example `goblin` or `undercommon`) are disclosed as removals before confirmation, excluded from the migrated copy so their points are available for reselection, and preserved on the locked legacy source record. --- ### Acceptance Criteria (Background) - Conversions follow documented formulas; over-budget states disable submit and surface errors. - Mastery cap validation emits `MASTERY_CAP_EXCEEDED` unless the allocation has a point-bought elevation or a feature/trait/talent cap increase. ## 4 Calculation Model Within `calculateCharacterWithBreakdowns`: - Base budgets (Level 1 defaults): - Skill Points = `5 + Intelligence + bonus('skillPoints')` - Trade Points = `3 + bonus('tradePoints')` - Language Points = `2 + bonus('languagePoints')` - Conversions applied: - `tradeToSkillUndo = min(tradeToSkill, skillToTrade*2)` - `effectiveSkillToTrade = skillToTrade - floor(tradeToSkillUndo/2)` - `availableSkillPoints = baseSkillPoints - effectiveSkillToTrade` - `availableTradePoints = baseTradePoints + effectiveSkillToTrade*2 - tradeToLanguage` - `availableLanguagePoints = baseLanguagePoints + tradeToLanguage*2` - Usage: - `skillPointsUsed = sum(levels in skillsData) + sum(spent skill mastery limit elevations)` - `tradePointsUsed = sum(levels in tradesData) + sum(spent trade mastery limit elevations)` - `languagePointsUsed = sum(fluency costs; limited=1, fluent=2; 'common' free)` - **Mastery Cap Validation** ✅ **NEW**: - Determines baseline mastery tier from character level - Identifies skills/trades exceeding baseline cap - Applies point-bought limit elevations from `skillMasteryLimitElevations` and `tradeMasteryLimitElevations` - Collects `MODIFY_SKILL_MASTERY_CAP` and `INCREASE_SKILL_MASTERY_CAP` effects - Validates feature/trait/talent increase budget and specific skill coverage - Generic feature cap grants, such as Human Skill Expertise, are allocated to over-baseline selections that do not already have a point-bought elevation; option-specific cap grants still conflict with point-bought elevations on the same Skill/Trade. - Emits `MASTERY_CAP_EXCEEDED` and `INVALID_MASTERY_GRANT` errors - A level 1 character can raise a Skill from no Mastery to Adept by spending 3 Skill Points: 1 for Novice, 1 to raise that Skill's limit, and 1 to raise the Skill's level to Adept. - Validation emits over-budget errors by step. Traits can modify these pools using effects: - `MODIFY_STAT` targets: `skillPoints`, `tradePoints`, `languagePoints` - **Mastery Cap Effects** ✅ **NEW**: - `MODIFY_SKILL_MASTERY_CAP` / `MODIFY_TRADE_MASTERY_CAP`: Grant specific tier unlocks - `INCREASE_SKILL_MASTERY_CAP` / `INCREASE_TRADE_MASTERY_CAP`: Increase cap by value - Class features can constrain cap increases with `options`; Cleric Knowledge Domain uses `INCREASE_TRADE_MASTERY_CAP` for Arcana, History, Nature, Occultism, and Religion. The calculator exposes a `background` block with: `{ baseSkillPoints, baseTradePoints, baseLanguagePoints, availableSkillPoints, availableTradePoints, availableLanguagePoints, skillPointsUsed, tradePointsUsed, languagePointsUsed, conversions }`. Denormalized outputs persisted on `SavedCharacter` (for UI/PDF consumption) — additive/optional fields introduced by Task 0: - `skillTotals: Record` - `skillMastery: Record` - `knowledgeTradeMastery: Record<'arcana'|'history'|'nature'|'occultism'|'religion', ...>` - `masteryLadders: { skills, knowledgeTrades, practicalTrades: { A..D: { label, ladder, finalValue } } }` - `languageMastery: { A..D: { name, limited, fluent } }` - `bloodiedValue`, `wellBloodiedValue`, and PD/AD heavy/brutal thresholds Transformer note: `src/lib/pdf/transformers.ts` reads these fields when present and only falls back to legacy math if they are missing, ensuring backward compatibility. Validation also exposes a `masteryLimits` block with: `{ maxSkillMastery, maxTradeMastery, currentAdeptCount, maxAdeptCount, canSelectAdept, baselineSkillCap, baselineTradeCap, skillEffectiveCaps, tradeEffectiveCaps, skillLimitElevations, tradeLimitElevations }`. --- ## 5 Adding/Modifying Background Data – Checklist ✅ 1. Data 1.1 Add or edit entries in `skills.ts`, `trades.ts`, or `languages.ts`. – Keep `id` stable; prefer kebab/underscore-free, lowercase IDs. – Ensure `attributeAssociation` is one of: `might | agility | charisma | intelligence | prime` (skills only). 2. Points & Conversions – To change defaults, update formulas in `enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts` (§4). – To add new conversion rules, extend the `conversions` structure in store and calculator consistently. 3. Trait Bonuses – Reuse `MODIFY_STAT` to target `skillPoints`, `tradePoints`, or `languagePoints`. – If a new pool is introduced, update `Effect.target` doc, calculator aggregation, and UI. 4. UI Wiring – UI components should read `calculationResult.background` and disable submit when over budget. – Languages: treat `common` as always fluent and free unless rules change. – Do not expose removed language names in selection UIs; if a legacy save uses an aliased ID, map it onto the current 0.10.5 language card. 5. Tests – Add unit tests for any formula changes or new conversions. – Run `npm run test:unit`. 6. Commit Message Template ``` feat(background): update definitions and budgets - rulesdata/.ts: +N updates - calculator: adjust background formulas - tests: add coverage for conversions and budgets ``` --- ## 6 Troubleshooting FAQ 🤖 | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Over-budget errors even with minimal choices | Conversion math or base budget regression | Re-check §4 formulas and state conversions wiring | | Language points miscounting | `common` included in cost | Ensure `common` is excluded from `languagePointsUsed` calc | | Trait background bonuses not applied | Missing `MODIFY_STAT` handling for pool target | Ensure target matches one of `skillPoints/tradePoints/languagePoints` | | New pool not reflected in UI | UI not reading calculator `background` | Update components to use `calculationResult.background` | --- ## 7 Future Evolution - Schema-driven editors for Skills/Trades/Languages. - ✅ **COMPLETED**: Mastery cap validation and granular control implemented - UI enhancements: Dynamic mastery cap indicators in skill/trade selection - TODO: Encode trait choice restrictions for Trade Expertise variants when the UI supports constrained background-effect choices. Current known restrictions include Dwarf (`Crafting or Services`) and Gnome (`Crafting or Subterfuge`). --- ## 8 DC20 v0.10.5 Audit Path - Rules version: `dc20-0.10.5` - Source artifact: `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md` - Generated report: `docs/migration/background-v0105-report.json` - Generate: `npm run background:generate:0105` - Validate report freshness: `npm run background:validate:0105` - Validate app data names: `npm run background:names:validate:0105` - Generate trait impact report: `npm run background:traits:generate:0105` - Validate trait impact report freshness: `npm run background:traits:validate:0105` Current report coverage: - 12 skills with source attributes. - 28 trades with tools and common attribute associations. - 15 selectable languages with family DCs. - Background budgets: 5 Skill Points plus Intelligence, 3 Trade Points, Common Fluency plus 2 Language Points. - Source conversions: `1 Skill Point -> 2 Trade Points`, `1 Trade Point -> 2 Language Points`. - `tradeToSkill` is bounded undo-only compatibility state, not a selectable rule conversion. - Background-affecting ancestry trait effects are reported in `docs/migration/background-trait-effects-v0105.json`. > Maintainer: @DC20Clean-Team

title: DC20Clean — Back Office
purpose: Private, read-only workspace for understanding system specifications and reviewing stored monsters.
owns: Reviewer access, system-document navigation and rendering, monster review queries, and back-office routes.
excludes: Rules interpretation, monster editing or approval, source imports, general user administration, or documentation authoring.
markdown:
# DC20Clean — Back Office

> Purpose: Private, read-only workspace for understanding system specifications and reviewing stored monsters.
> Owns: Reviewer access, system-document navigation and rendering, monster review queries, and back-office routes.
> Does not own: Rules interpretation, monster editing or approval, source imports, general user administration, or documentation authoring.
> Authoritative source: `convex/backOffice.ts`, `convex/lib/backOfficeAccess.ts`, `src/routes/back-office/`, and `scripts/back-office/generateSystems.mjs`.
> Related systems: [Architecture](./PROJECT_TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.MD), [Database](./DATABASE_SYSTEM.MD), [Monsters](./MONSTER_SYSTEM_SPEC.MD), [Testing](./TESTING_SYSTEM.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-10-02

## 1. Access and routes

1. `/back-office` and `/back-office/systems` open the system reader; `/back-office/systems/:documentId` opens a specific Markdown specification.
2. `/back-office/monsters` opens the monster list; `/back-office/monsters/:monsterId` uses the Convex document ID to open a stored stat block.
3. Access requires real Convex authentication and a server-owned user record with a verified email matching `yasaf.vol@gmail.com` or `nzinger@gmail.com` (Nir Zinger). Client-provided identity, local mode, and `VITE_BYPASS_AUTH` cannot grant access.
4. `backOffice.access` returns only a boolean. Every content query independently checks access before reading data or returning documents. Unknown, signed-out, and unverified accounts receive no review content.
5. The menu and homepage navigation expose the Back office link only after server confirmation. Direct links display sign-in, restricted-access, loading, unavailable-record, and query-failure states as appropriate. A missing back-office query displays a specific backend deployment message.
6. The workspace exports no mutations. It does not confer rights to existing monster mutation functions.
7. Vite development mode alone exposes `/back-office-preview`. It reuses the same reader and stat-block presentation with checkout system text and explicitly synthetic monsters. It uses no Convex queries, account access, or persistent data. The separate `/back-office` route keeps its server access checks. Production builds omit the preview route, fixture module, and system snapshot from browser assets.

## 2. System reader

1. `docs/systems/` remains the documentation authority. The reader does not author or rewrite these files.
2. `systemNavigation.ts` supplies three overlapping reading views:
   1. Verticals: character building, rules and equipment, and the DM workspace.
   2. Flows: build/save/play, progression/upgrade/export, and monster/encounter/campaign preparation.
   3. Horizontals: shared mechanics, data/compatibility, and platform/quality.
3. These are curated navigation paths. They do not assert a complete FITL architecture or introduce another behavior specification. Horizontals here means shared systems; FITL's architectural layers are not relabeled as systems.
4. Search matches the full Markdown across all active documents and combines with the optional selected area. Without an area filter every specification remains discoverable, including newly added files.
5. Metadata displays purpose, ownership, exclusions, authority, and the recorded update date. Missing metadata is shown as unrecorded, not inferred.
6. The reader supports headings, an on-page outline, fenced code, lists, tables, and links between known system documents. External HTTP(S) links open separately. Other repository references are displayed without pretending that they are application pages. Raw HTML is not executed.
7. `backoffice:generate` snapshots only Markdown files directly under `docs/systems/` into `convex/backOfficeData/systems.json`. The snapshot is imported solely by the protected backend, never by public browser bundles or static assets.
8. `predev`, `prebuild`, and `preconvex:dev` regenerate the snapshot. `backoffice:check` detects drift. Direct Convex deployment commands must run `npm run backoffice:generate` first so the backend receives current documentation. Frontend builds alone do not update deployed Convex content.

## 3. Monster review

1. Reviewers can read active official, custom, and homebrew monsters across owners, including private and pending records. Soft-deleted records are excluded from both lists and details.
2. Lists use bounded reactive pagination, 30 initial records and at most 50 per backend page. Name search uses a Convex search index; role/tier filters apply to the complete query, not just loaded rows. Empty-search queries use indexes for the active filter combination.
3. Detail displays persisted HP, PD, AD, attack, save DC, damage, attributes, feature points, actions, descriptions, lore, tactics, visibility, and approval state. It does not recalculate, migrate, or save monsters.
4. Referenced features are resolved by application ID using the indexed feature catalog, preferring official entries, then the monster owner's entries, then approved public entries. Missing references are explicitly visible.
5. Existing fork metadata is displayed when available. The current monster schema has no source-document/page fields; the reader explicitly displays the absence of a stored source reference rather than assigning a publication or page.
6. Search and filters survive opening a detail link. A missing, deleted, or invalid record cannot produce an editable designer.

## 4. Verification

1. `convex/backOffice.test.ts` proves both reviewers' access, signed-out/unverified/other-account denial on every content query, pagination, complete-query role/tier filtering, search, deleted-record exclusion, and feature-reference resolution.
2. Reader navigation tests check document coverage and system-link resolution; UI tests check access states, system/monster review interactions, and overflow at phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
3. Verify the production browser bundle contains no system snapshot text. Backend deployment and authorized live sign-in are separate from local implementation verification.
4. The local preview tests check navigation, filtering, detail rendering, and absence of Convex content queries without sign-in. This preview verifies presentation only; backend access behavior remains covered by the protected query tests.

purpose: Definitive guide to derived stat formulas, effect application order, mastery cap validation, and breakdown output.
