markdown:
# DC20Clean – Character Sheet

> Purpose: End-to-end map of Character Sheet UI: architecture, components, data sources, and interactions.
> Owns: Character-sheet state and presentation, in-play resource controls, sheet actions, auto-save coordination, responsive layouts, and read-only rendering.
> Does not own: Character-creation rules, derived-stat formulas, persistence implementations, campaign authorization, or PDF field mapping.
> Authoritative source: `src/routes/character-sheet/`, especially `hooks/CharacterSheetProvider.tsx`, the sheet reducer, and section components.
> Related systems: [Alternative Presentation](./ALTERNATIVE_CHARACTER_SHEET.MD), [Calculation](./CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD), [Database](./DATABASE_SYSTEM.MD), [Campaigns](./CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD), [PDF Export](./PDF_EXPORT_SYSTEM.MD), [Conditions](./CONDITIONS_SYSTEM.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-20

## Recent UX additions

Alternative-only composition and interaction detail is maintained in
`ALTERNATIVE_CHARACTER_SHEET.MD`; this document remains authoritative for shared sheet
state, behavior, and ownership.

- **Responsive contract**: The live menu and primary sheet use two shared viewport thresholds from `src/styles/responsive.ts`: tablet begins at 768px and desktop begins at 1200px. Compact layouts are the base below 768px; tablet layouts occupy 768–1199px; desktop layouts begin at 1200px. Component internals use fluid grids, wrapping, intrinsic minimums, and container queries instead of additional viewport breakpoints. The primary sheet keeps a stable 280px attribute column above the compact threshold. Spell and Maneuver rows switch between labelled cards and full table rows according to the tab container's available width, so crossing 1200px does not force a cramped table.
- **Alternative sheet route**: `/character2/:id` renders the incremental alternative sheet under the same `CharacterSheetProvider`; `/character2/` resolves the most recently modified saved character. Every saved-character card on `/load-character` offers separate `View Sheet` and `Alternative Sheet` actions, with the current sheet remaining the default. The alternative sheet currently contains the identity/action header, horizontal HP/Mana/Stamina/Rest/Grit strip, an attribute-mastery section, a full-width combat strip, and a tabbed action/detail panel below them. The panel reuses the existing Attacks, Spells, Inventory, Maneuvers, Features, Conditions, and Notes content; its tab bar remains horizontally scrollable on narrow screens and switches content without entry animation. The active tab supplies the section label, so the alternative sheet suppresses each reused panel's duplicate top-level title while retaining controls, category headings, and active counts. The mastery section groups every Skill under its governing Attribute, assigns each selected Trade to its highest valid Attribute total, keeps Awareness under Prime, and sends Attribute Saves, Skills, and Trades to the shared automatic Dice Roller with active-condition modifiers. The combat strip gives Attack primary-action hierarchy; aligns Save DC, Initiative, and Jump as equal tactical metrics; and shows Walk plus calculator-returned movement modes in a stable Walk, Climb, Swim, Fly, Burrow, Glide order. PD and AD use compact rows whose Hit baseline is dominant, with Heavy +5 and Brutal +10 separated by scale, tone, and accent color above a shared PDR/EDR/MDR footer. Read-only PDR/EDR/MDR indicators are sourced from categorical resistance grants. Attack and Initiative send to the same Dice Roller. It reuses `StatCard`, the existing reducer mutations, Long Rest behavior, campaign-feed action, stored-value PDF export, JSON export, and Rulebook article links. Mana and Stamina are each omitted when their maximum is zero. Alternative-sheet `StatCard` instances skip mount fade and initial bar-fill transitions while retaining value-change and control feedback. This route adds no schema or persistence path.
- **Alternative section disclosure**: Resources; Attributes, Skills & Trades; Combat; and Actions & Details each have a visible section heading and an independent disclosure control. All four sections start expanded at every viewport size. Collapsing hides the mounted content immediately without a slide animation, so local tab and row-edit state survives reopening.
- **Alternative sheet color roles**: Structural surfaces and passive values stay neutral; crystal blue identifies roll actions and interaction states; each Attribute color is limited to its title, top border, and filled mastery dots; both defenses use the purple defense family; resource colors retain their established meanings; green is reserved for active positive states such as damage reduction.
- **Alternative tab interaction**: Subtle dividers separate the uppercase tabs; the active tab uses a crystal-tinted surface, inset outline, and thicker top accent. Existing editable rows in Attacks, Spells, Inventory, Maneuvers, and Notes use a trailing pencil to enter edit mode, check to finish, and delete only while editing. Add Weapon, Add Spell, Add Maneuver, and Add Item open alternative pickers and create populated rows only after confirmation. Features and Conditions retain their existing view/control behavior.
- **Contextual rules tabs**: Spells and Maneuvers appear only when their calculated known-slot/budget entitlement is positive or the saved character already contains an entry. The saved-entry fallback keeps legacy data reachable when current calculation is unavailable.
- **Hero strip restructured to fluid columns**: `HeroSection` uses a container-driven layout:
  - **Col 1**: Health (HP + Temp HP + Health Status + Exhaustion) — unchanged.
  - **Col 2**: Resources (Mana and Stamina) above Recovery (Rest and Grit).
  - **Col 3**: Combat Stats with compact movement, currency, senses, resistances, vulnerabilities, and combat training.
  - Cards keep an 18rem intrinsic minimum and move between three, two, and one columns according to the width available inside the sheet, without adding viewport breakpoints.
  - Mana/Stamina and Rest/Grit remain two equal inner columns, and the three defense values remain one equal row, at every hero width that renders the desktop/tablet sheet.
- **Resource controls**: Editable HP, Mana, Stamina, Rest, Grit, and Temp HP values place decrement/increment controls directly around the value (`− current / max +`); current and maximum values use equal-sized, equal-width tabular numeral slots around a centered separator, so different digit counts and negative HP do not unbalance the control. The primary sheet's paired Mana/Stamina and Rest/Grit cards use smaller controls, type, and spacing so the separator remains legible in their narrow columns; the alternative sheet retains the standard layout. The alternative sheet stretches every resource card to the tallest card in its row and reserves an equal-height status row in every card, keeping all progress bars aligned. The calculated Health Status chip sits close beneath the HP label with separation from the value. The redundant “Main” label is removed. In the Health card, Temp HP is an unframed standalone control below the HP progress bar; changing it never changes current or maximum HP. The bar reserves 25% of its width for negative HP and 75% for normal HP, with a subtle zero marker between them; negative HP fills and animates leftward from zero in alert red. Current HP and Temp HP render as separate resource-coloured and yellow segments. Damage consumes Temp HP first, then HP. HP can decrease to the calculated negative Death Threshold.
- **Resource row layout**: The disclosure header sits outside a nested `auto-fit` card grid, so only visible resource cards determine the column count and divide the full row equally.
- **HP formula tooltip**: HP hover keeps the shared tabular calculation tooltip, but dynamically splits calculator base HP into class progression (`Level · Class`) and Might rows, followed by every source-attributed HP modifier such as ancestry traits, class features, talents, and equipped items. A second table shows the displayed negative Death Threshold as Prime Attribute + Combat Mastery + source-attributed modifiers.
- **Hero card hierarchy**: The hero strip omits redundant Health, Resources, Recovery, and Combat Stats headings. Conditional reset actions remain available without reserving header space when no override exists.
- **Compact resource labels**: Hero resource cards use Hit Points, Mana, Stamina, Rest, and Grit without the redundant “Points” suffix.
- **Defense cards**: Combat Stats uses the canonical labels PD, Damage Reduction, and AD. Both PD and AD show Heavy and Brutal thresholds on separate lines using defense +5/+10. On the alternative sheet, hovering the PD or AD abbreviation shows the canonical formula, its live component values, active source-attributed bonuses, and any displayed override.
- **Attribute headers**: Might, Agility, Charisma, and INT use a compact `Attribute ±score (±save save)` reading order; duplicate abbreviation boxes are removed while score tooltips and clickable save rolls remain intact.
- **Prime hierarchy**: Prime occupies the first column beside the four Attributes, uses their exact header structure and spacing, and owns Awareness. Compact Combat Mastery sits directly beneath Prime. Mana Spend Limit and the Mana resource consume one provider-owned visibility fact derived from calculated maximum Mana. A Meta Magic exemption chip and exception text appear only when the provider resolves the canonical Meta Magic feature ID, including a multiclass grant. Both cards use purple top-border accents, with Combat Mastery using a 30%-lighter treatment. Awareness and every Attribute skill list share the same top baseline.
- **CompactUtility component** (`components/new/CompactUtility.tsx`): compact replacement for the old Utility tab:

## 1. Architecture

The character sheet uses a **context provider pattern** with a reducer for state management:

1. `CharacterSheetRouter.tsx` ? entry point; wraps everything in `CharacterSheetProvider`
2. `CharacterSheetProvider` (in `hooks/`) ? loads character from storage, checks compatibility, runs `calculateCharacterWithBreakdowns()` once per character state when full recalculation is allowed, and provides both calculated data and normalized sheet-presentation facts through context. Mana visibility, spell access, maneuver access, and canonical Meta Magic eligibility are resolved here rather than independently inside section components.
3. `useCharacterSheetReducer` ? reducer for local sheet state (resource changes, condition toggles, inventory edits)
4. Layout components render sections based on breakpoint

**Data flow**: Storage ? `CharacterSheetProvider` ? compatibility classifier ? calculator/context ? section components

Compatibility states from the rules-version fence affect sheet persistence:

| State              | Sheet behavior                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `editable`         | Normal render and full auto-save with recalculated values                                                                                   |
| `upgrade-required` | Stored-value render/export; only HP, Temp HP, MP, SP, Rest, Grit, and Exhaustion controls remain active and auto-save without recalculation |
| `view-only`        | Render allowed where possible; auto-save is disabled                                                                                        |

For `upgrade-required` and `view-only` characters, the sheet suppresses fresh calculator output for display/export helpers that would reinterpret the character under the current rules data. PDF export always uses stored `SavedCharacter` values for every rules version; it does not recalculate during export.

## 8. Read-Only Mode (Campaign Viewing)

Campaign members can view a shared character in read-only mode through either the Primary or Alternative presentation. The presentation does not own the campaign connection: both render the same authorized record under one `CharacterSheetProvider`.

### 8.1 Trigger

`CharacterSheetProvider` accepts `campaignId?: string` and `campaignCharacterDocId?: string`. `campaignId` enables read-only mode; the optional record ID selects the exact campaign roster record.

`CampaignCharacterView` owns the presentation switch. The default is Primary; `?sheet=alternative` selects Alternative while preserving the campaign and exact character-record parameters.

```typescript
<CharacterSheetProvider campaignId={campaignId} characterId={characterId} campaignCharacterDocId={characterDocId} />
```

### 8.2 Load path

When `campaignId` is present, the character is fetched via the guarded `characters.getByIdForMember` query rather than local storage. Current roster links pass both the app ID and Convex record ID; the backend requires them to identify the same connected record.

```typescript
const campaignCharacter = useQuery(
	api.characters.getByIdForMember,
	campaignId ? { campaignId, characterId, characterDocId } : 'skip'
);
```

### 8.3 No save effects

- The auto-save `useEffect` short-circuits when a campaign view is active.
- `saveNow` is a no-op: `if (readOnly) return`.
- `retryFailedSave` is guarded: `if (readOnly || !state.character) return`.

### 8.4 Reducer no-op guards

`useCharacterSheetReducer` distinguishes full editing from resource management. Campaign views allow neither. Upgrade-required owners allow only the seven live resource callbacks. All structural callbacks remain no-ops.

The Attacks, Inventory, Spells, Maneuvers, Conditions, and Notes panels suppress mutation controls in read-only mode. Inventory detail popups render custom fields as values instead of inputs; filtering, detail expansion, and presentation navigation remain available.

### 8.5 Presentation controls and banners

`CampaignCharacterView.tsx` renders common navigation, a Primary/Alternative switch, and a read-only label. `CharacterSheetRedesign.tsx` also renders its existing banner when `readOnly` is truthy:

```
Read-only — viewing <characterName>'s sheet
```

### 8.6 Related files

| File                                                          | Role                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `src/routes/character-sheet/hooks/CharacterSheetProvider.tsx` | `readOnly` flag, load path, save guards        |
| `src/routes/character-sheet/CharacterSheetRedesign.tsx`       | Read-only banner                               |
| `src/routes/campaigns/CampaignCharacterView.tsx`              | Shared read-only route and presentation switch |
| `convex/characters.ts` (`getByIdForMember`)                   | Three-layer guarded query                      |

See `docs/systems/CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD` for the full campaign architecture.

---

## 9. Related Docs

- `docs/systems/ALTERNATIVE_CHARACTER_SHEET.MD` — alternative-only presentation contract
- `docs/systems/CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD` — how stats are computed
- `docs/systems/SPELLS_SYSTEM.MD` — spell data and assignment
- `docs/systems/MARTIALS_SYSTEM.MD` — maneuver data
- `docs/systems/BACKGROUND_SYSTEM.MD` — skills/trades/languages
- `docs/systems/CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD` — campaign system and read-only mode

ClassSelector.tsx
ClassFeatures.tsx
CharacterSheetProvider.tsx] end C1 --> D1 --> D2 --> D3 ``` --- ## 2 Key Files & Their Roles | Layer | File / Dir | Responsibility | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Features** | `classes-data/features/*_features.ts` (13 files) | Declarative definition of each class's core & subclass features | | **Progressions** | `classes-data/progressions/classProgressionDefinitions.ts` | Central runtime progression model: each class declares `fullMartial`, `fullCaster`, or `hybrid`, plus feature schedule and optional full explicit source table | | | `classes-data/progressions/*.progression.ts` (13 files) | Thin public exports that resolve the class table from `classProgressionDefinitions.ts` | | **Progression Templates** | `classes-data/progressions/templates/` | Shared source-of-truth category tables: `martial.template.ts`, `caster.template.ts`, `spellblade.template.ts`, plus `createClassProgression()` for feature schedule overlay | | **Talents** | `classes-data/talents/*.talents.ts` (13 class files) | Per-class talent definitions with prerequisites and effects | | **Talent Infrastructure** | `classes-data/talents/talent.types.ts` | `Talent` interface, `TalentCategory`, `TalentPrerequisites` | | | `classes-data/talents/talent.loader.ts` | Loads and indexes talents by class | | | `classes-data/talents/talents.data.ts` | Combined talent data export | | **Progression Resolver** | `classes-data/classProgressionResolver.ts` | Resolves progression up to target level; returns budgets, features, choices | | **Class Utilities** | `classes-data/classUtils.ts` | Helper functions for class/subclass data lookup | | **Progression Types** | `classes-data/progressionTypes.ts` | `ClassProgressionGains`, `ClassProgressionLevel` interfaces | | **Type Contracts** | `schemas/types.ts` | TS interfaces `IClassDefinition`, `IClassFeature`, `IClassFeatureChoice` | | | `schemas/class.schema.ts` | Zod schema for validation & effect typing | | **Validation** | `loaders/class.loader.ts` | Loads progression, features, `spellRestrictions`; validates against schema | | | `rulesdata.spec.ts` | Unit test asserting every class passes schema | | **v0.10.5 Audit** | `scripts/classes/dc20-0105-classes.mjs` | Extracts the class source report from `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md` | | | `scripts/classes/dc20-0105-class-effects.ts` | Classifies runtime class feature effects against calculator/stat/display paths | | | `scripts/classes/dc20-0105-class-audit-report.mjs` | Generates the human-readable class feature audit markdown | | | `docs/migration/classes-v0105-report.json` | Generated source comparison report for core classes | | | `docs/migration/class-feature-effect-classification.json` | Generated implementation coverage report for runtime class feature effects | | | `docs/migration/class-feature-audit.md` | Human-readable per-class report covering features, selections, and effects | | | `classes-data/classesSource.test.ts` | Focused source/runtime/effect report validation | | **Runtime** | `services/enhancedCharacterCalculator.ts` | Aggregates class effects, resolves choices, outputs stats | | **State** | `stores/characterContext.tsx`, `hooks/useCharacterBuilder.ts` | Provides calculated results to UI | | **UI** | `routes/character-creation/*` (selection), `routes/character-sheet/*` (display) | Imports `classesData` / `classFeaturesData` | All paths above are relative to `src/lib/rulesdata/` unless otherwise noted. --- ## 3 Adding **New Class** – Checklist ✅ 1. **Data** 1.1 Add an entry to `classes-data/progressions/classProgressionDefinitions.ts`. ‑ Set `category` to `fullMartial`, `fullCaster`, or `hybrid`. ‑ Add class-specific feature IDs in `featureSchedule`, normally levels 1, 2, 5, and 9. ‑ Provide `explicitProgression` only when the source publishes a class table that differs from the category table. Explicit progression must be a full 10-row table, not a partial patch. 1.2 Create progression file: `classes-data/progressions/.progression.ts`. ‑ Export `Progression` by calling `resolveClassProgressionTable('')`. 1.3 Create feature file: `classes-data/features/_features.ts` exporting `Class` that conforms to `ClassDefinition`. ‑ Include `coreFeatures`, `subclasses`, and any starting equipment blocks. 1.4 Add class metadata to `class.loader.ts` CLASS_METADATA constant. 2. **Names & IDs** ‑ `className` (PascalCase) must match table file and UI strings. ‑ Exported constant should follow the `Class` pattern (e.g., `paladinClass`). 3. **Effects** ‑ Re-use existing `effect.type` strings whenever possible (see `docs/systems/EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD`). ‑ If a genuinely new mechanic is required, see §4 before merging. 4. **Types / Schema** ‑ Add new `effect.type` to `class.schema.ts` **and** `types.ts` as needed. ‑ Update any calculator logic (usually in `createStatBreakdown`). 5. **Calculator Support** ‑ Numeric buffs → update stat aggregation helpers. ‑ Abilities (actions, reactions) → emit as `GRANT_ABILITY` (no engine change). 6. **UI** ‑ Components auto-render from data; images/icons may be added under `assets/` if desired. 7. **Tests** ‑ Run `npm run test:unit`; `rulesdata.spec.ts` should pass. ‑ Add dedicated calculation tests for complex mechanics. 8. **Docs** ‑ Append a bullet to this file under “Next Classes Added”. 9. **Commit Message Template** ``` feat(rules): add class & N core features - *_features.ts: +N entries - *.progression.ts: new file - tests: update counts ``` --- ## 4 Talent System Talents are level-up choices that grant additional effects. They are defined per-class in `classes-data/talents/`. ### Talent Data Shape (`talent.types.ts`) ```typescript type TalentCategory = 'General' | 'Class' | 'Multiclass'; interface TalentPrerequisites { level?: number; classId?: string; feature?: string; otherFeature?: string; subclass?: string; other?: string; } interface Talent { id: string; name: string; category: TalentCategory; description: string; effects: Effect[]; prerequisites: TalentPrerequisites; stackable?: boolean; } ``` ### Talent Files Each class has a `.talents.ts` file (13 files) plus shared data in `talents.data.ts`. The `talent.loader.ts` loads and indexes them by class. ### Adding a New Talent 1. Add entry to the appropriate `.talents.ts` file 2. Set `category` to `General`, `Class`, or `Multiclass` 3. Define `prerequisites` (level, classId, feature, subclass) 4. Define `effects` using existing effect types from `EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD` 5. Set `stackable: true` if the talent can be taken multiple times 6. Run `npm run test:unit` — talent tests in `talents.test.ts` should pass --- ## 5 Adding **New Class Feature Effect Type** – Decision Matrix | Question | Yes | No | | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | | Does an existing `effect.type` cover the mechanic? | Use it → go to Step 3 | Create new type → continue | | Does the effect alter a **numeric stat**? | Implement in calculator (`createStatBreakdown`) | Use `GRANT_ABILITY` + manual rules text | | Does the UI need to resolve **user choice**? | Add `userChoiceRequired` in feature & update `resolveEffectChoices` | — | **When a new type is created:** 1. Extend `IClassFeature.effects[].type` JSDoc comment (open list). 2. Extend Zod schema validation. 3. Implement logic in calculator. 4. Write unit test(s). --- ## 6 Troubleshooting FAQ | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | **Vite import error** for class files | File path typo (`classes-data/...`) | Check `import ... classFeaturesData` paths | | New class not visible in UI | Missing `_features.ts` or `.progression.ts` file, or missing CLASS_METADATA | Verify file names, exported constant, and metadata | | Unit test `rulesdata.spec.ts` fails | Schema violation (missing field / wrong effect) | Inspect test output & update data | | Stats not updating for new effect | Effect type not handled in calculator | Add case to `createStatBreakdown` | | Feature choice dropdown empty | `choices` array missing `options` | Populate `options` with `label` & `value` fields | --- ## 7 Future Evolution -- Effect Processor integration will unify class & ancestry effect handling—update §3 Step 4 when landed. - **Subclass-driven UI**: dynamic forms may auto-render based on schema. - **Data-driven progression editor** planned; stay tuned. --- ## 8 DC20 v0.10.5 Notes **Level Cap**: DC20 v0.10.5 is a level 1-10 system (not 1-20). All class progressions have 10 levels. **Classes Available** (13 feature files): - Martial: Barbarian, Champion, Commander, Hunter, Monk, Rogue - Caster: Bard, Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard - Hybrid: Spellblade **Key v0.10.5 Progression Contract**: - Martial starting resources: 2 SP at level 1. - Spellcaster starting resources: 6 MP at level 1, with +3 MP at levels 3, 5, 7, 9, and 10. - Hybrid starting resources: Spellblade starts with 1 SP and 3 MP, then totals 3 SP and 11 MP by level 10. - Runtime derives numeric resources, talent/path/ancestry timing, and subclass-choice timing from the class's progression category unless the class has a full explicit source progression table. - Per-class progression files are stubs over `resolveClassProgressionTable('')`. - Current explicit progression tables: Rogue and Warlock. Both differ from their category defaults in HP gains. - Category-derived classes provide only the feature IDs that occupy the class-feature slots. - Talent grants are not class features. Keep `gains.talents` in the shared progression templates and do not add generic `Talent` feature records to `classes-data/features/*_features.ts`. - Shared feature schedule: - Level 1: Class Features - Level 2: Class Feature, Talent, Path Progression - Level 3: Subclass Feature - Level 4: Talent, 2 Ancestry Points, Path Progression - Level 5: Class Expert Feature - Level 6: Talent, Path Progression - Level 7: Subclass Expert Feature - Level 8: Talent, 2 Ancestry Points, Path Progression - Level 9: Class Capstone Feature - Level 10: Subclass Capstone Feature **Level 5 Expert Feature Contract**: - Every implemented v0.10.5 class resolves a level 5 Expert Feature from the existing persisted ID shape (`_level_5_placeholder`). - Those IDs are intentionally retained as compatibility aliases for saved v0.10 characters and progression references; only the displayed feature name, description, benefits, and modeled effects changed. - Universal mechanical benefits use existing effect types (`MODIFY_STAT`, `GRANT_SPELL`, `GRANT_MANEUVERS`, `GRANT_ABILITY`) so character creation, sheet rendering, calculator breakdowns, and PDF export consume the same data path. **Level 9 Class Capstone Contract**: - The bundled v0.10.5 source tables schedule a Class Capstone Feature at level 9, but do not publish class-specific capstone mechanics. - Runtime class data does not include source-unpublished capstone placeholders. - Do not invent class capstone mechanics from names, table labels, or older placeholder text. Add level 9 class capstones only when a source publishes mechanics. **v0.10.5 Audit Path**: ```bash npm run classes:generate:0105 npm run classes:effects:generate npm run classes:audit:generate npm run classes:validate:0105 npm run classes:effects:validate npm run classes:audit:validate npm run test:unit -- --project server --run src/lib/rulesdata/classes-data/classesSource.test.ts ``` - `docs/migration/classes-v0105-report.json` is the source-derived class report: core class list, detailed class tables, starting equipment, paths, subclass choices, and broad `coreFeatureCandidates`. - `docs/migration/class-feature-effect-classification.json` is the runtime implementation coverage report for class feature effects. - `docs/migration/class-feature-audit.md` is the readable report grouped alphabetically by class, then feature, selection, and effect. - The class audit fails focused tests when any feature has duplicate always-on effects across direct feature effects and benefit effects. Choice-option effects are excluded from this duplicate check. - Runtime exposes 13 core class feature definitions: Barbarian, Bard, Champion, Cleric, Commander, Druid, Hunter, Monk, Rogue, Sorcerer, Spellblade, Warlock, Wizard. - The clean v0.10.5 source has detailed class chapters for 12 of those runtime classes. Cleric is listed as core but has no detailed class chapter in the parsed class source range. - Source feature extraction uses broad candidates because the cleaned markdown uses flat `##` headings for both real feature names and nested option headings. Runtime validation matches implemented L1/L2/L5 non-placeholder features against those candidates. - Effect coverage categories are `calculated`, `collected`, `choice-tracked`, `progression-derived`, `partial`, and `uncovered`. `calculated` feeds numeric/stat/resource/spell/maneuver output; `collected` means the sheet/calculator gathers the effect for display/use. `text-only-no-effects` and `flavor-no-effects` are failing audit states: non-progression class features need at least one structured effect, even if that effect is only a collected rules note. - Combat Training from class paths uses canonical effect targets from the source audit: `Weapons`, `Spell_Focuses`, `Light_Armor`, `Heavy_Armor`, `All_Armor`, `Light_Shields`, `Heavy_Shields`, and `All_Shields`. Focused resolver tests compare every class against the v0.10.5 source list. **Champion Fighting Spirit Contract**: - v0.10.5 renames the Champion Fighting Spirit option `Brace` to `Fortify` to avoid confusion with the still-current Brace maneuver. - `Advance` now grants ADV on the next Martial Attack or Physical Check. - The rulesdata effect target is `combat_readiness_fortify`; legacy references to `combat_readiness_brace` are treated as a feature alias, not a maneuver alias. **Removed Talent Contract**: - `Swift Berserker` is removed from v0.10.5 selection and marked deprecated in `barbarian.talents.ts`. - Deprecated talents remain in `allTalents` and `findTalentById()` so old saved characters can still load, render, calculate existing effects, and export. - Character creation uses `selectableTalents`, which filters deprecated talents out of new or level-up choices. **Key Changes from v0.9.5/v0.10**: - Techniques have been removed entirely from the game - Spell schools reorganized to 8 schools (Astromancy, Conjuration, Divination, Elemental, Enchantment, Invocation, Nullification, Transmutation) - Spell lists removed; spells are accessed by source (Arcane/Divine/Primal) and school - Class features updated with new effects and descriptions - **Slot-Based Spell System (M3.20)**: Classes define individual Spell slots ("Pockets"), supporting highly specific restrictions (e.g., expanded schools) alongside broad global magic profiles. Current progression grants Spells only; legacy imported cantrip fields are normalized at the compatibility boundary. - **Current Spell-Grant Contract**: Current class, subclass, and talent data author only `GRANT_SPELL` and use Spell terminology. Wild Speech grants Druidcraft through `GRANT_SPELL`; legacy effect tokens and class-path metadata remain accepted only at compatibility boundaries. - **Data-Driven Spell Restrictions**: Classes now define `spellRestrictions` (allowed sources, schools, and tags) to automatically filter available spells in the character creator. **Recent Updates (2026-06-01)**: - **Level 5 Expert Features**: Replaced all level 5 class placeholders with explicit v0.10.5 Expert Feature blocks while preserving the legacy placeholder IDs for saved-character compatibility. - **v0.10.5 Progression Tables**: Updated caster MP gains, Spellblade starting/capstone MP, and levels 6-10 feature/talent/path/ancestry schedule. - **Champion Fighting Spirit**: Updated Combat Readiness to use `Fortify` and Advance's Martial Attack / Physical Check wording while preserving the Brace maneuver as a separate current maneuver. - **Feature Semantics Pass**: Updated Elemental Blast, Cleric, Commander, Monk, Rogue, and Spellblade feature text/effects to the source-confirmed v0.10.5 behavior while preserving existing feature IDs. - **Swift Berserker Removal**: Deprecated Swift Berserker for compatibility lookup while hiding it from current character creation selections. - **Path Progression Display**: `class.loader.ts` now surfaces `pathProgression: true` as "Path Progression" in formatted level rows. - **Progression Tests**: Added v0.10.5 resolver coverage for caster/hybrid MP totals, level 6-10 schedule, and level 5 Expert Feature coverage/effects. **Recent Updates (2026-06-13)**: - **Starting Equipment Migration**: Canonical class data now stores v0.10.5 starting equipment in structured `startingEquipment` blocks using `arsenal`, `spellFocuses`, `armor`, `tradeTools`, and `packs`, with conditional Heavy Armor/Heavy Shield language preserved where the source ties it to specific level-1 feature choices. - **Class Spell/Training Grants**: Exact spell grants now resolve to canonical generated spell IDs, unresolved class spell choices no longer create unrestricted slots, Wizard/Sorcerer/Warlock/Druid grant `Spell_Focuses` training, and Cleric Chastise / Hand of Salvation render as granted abilities. - **Intro Flavor Guard**: Monk, Rogue, and Spellblade `Source of Power` flavor entries are excluded from automatic multiclass flavor-feature grants. - **Level 9 Capstone Source Gap**: Source-unpublished class capstone placeholders were removed. Level 9 class capstones should be added only when class-specific source mechanics exist. **Recent Updates (2026-06-22)**: - **Duplicate Always-On Effect Audit**: Class feature audit reports and tests now flag duplicate always-on effects across direct feature effects and benefit effects. Barbarian Martial Path combat training now lives only under its `Combat Training` benefit, removing duplicate Weapons/Armor/Shields grants from runtime combat-training output. - **Barbarian Runtime Effects**: Rage sheet toggles now feed the calculator `while_raging` condition. Berserker Defense applies from the inferred `not_wearing_armor` condition when no equipped armor row exists. Mighty Leap's `SET_VALUE:jumpCalculationAttribute=might` is calculator-backed and uses the higher of Might or Agility for Jump Distance. - **Rage Sheet Resolution**: Rage's `martial_melee_damage` effect applies to supported Unarmed Strike and melee weapon rows while active; ranged and unresolved custom rows remain unchanged. The alternative sheet also applies Rage ADV to Might Saves, shows the PD penalty through calculator output, and discloses the complete base feature rule. - **Talent Feature Cleanup**: Generic level-2 `Talent` pseudo-features were removed from class feature data. Talent budgets now come only from shared progression template `gains.talents`, and level-up selection still consumes `selectedTalents`. - **Combat Training Source Alignment**: Bard, Monk, Rogue, Champion, and conditional Cleric/Spellblade training are covered by source-aligned `GRANT_COMBAT_TRAINING` tests. Monk/Rogue now expose their missing Martial Path feature records, and Champion uses canonical `All_Armor`. - **Martial Path Maneuver Source**: Martial Path maneuver access, including learning all Attack Maneuvers, is represented by class path/progression data (`martialPath.maneuvers`) rather than direct class feature effects. Commander and Hunter Martial Path feature effects now only collect combat training plus class-specific stamina regen where present. - **Commander Natural Leader**: Natural Leader stores the full v0.10.5 source text and models its check-ADV clauses with `GRANT_ADV_ON_CHECK`; the calculator collects these as sheet-facing advantage notes rather than applying automatic roll math. - **No Text-Only Feature Contract**: Class features should not remain prose-only. Descriptive or in-game-only mechanics use collected effects such as `GRANT_ABILITY` or `GRANT_ADV_ON_CHECK`; choice options should carry selected-option note effects when they have no calculator-backed mechanic. `classesSource.test.ts` fails if `text-only-no-effects` or `flavor-no-effects` reappears in the generated class effect report. - **Cleric Domain Effects**: Knowledge now raises the five Knowledge Trade mastery caps through `INCREASE_TRADE_MASTERY_CAP`; Darkvision is range-aware and handles "10 Spaces, or +5 if already present"; Divination uses condition immunity for Flanked; nonnumeric domains are collected as granted abilities. - **Hunter Subterranean Senses**: Subterranean Favored Terrain uses the same range-aware sense pattern as Cleric Dark Domain: Darkvision grants 10 or increases existing Darkvision by 5, and Tremorsense grants 3 or increases existing Tremorsense by 2. - **Monk Stance TODO**: Monk Stances are currently selected text with no active sheet model. A future character-sheet benefits surface should expose the selected stance benefits and support active-state presentation for nuanced effects such as stance damage bonuses, ADV notes, movement changes, and reductions. Rage now has its own alternative-sheet control and is not part of this remaining stance work. - **Spellblade Progression-Derived Paths**: Spellblade Martial Path and Spellcasting Path feature records are marked `isProgressionDerived` and carry no duplicate feature effects. The hybrid progression grants both martial and spellcasting table benefits; the class-specific stamina regen remains on `martialPath.staminaRegen` as collected in-game text. - **Warlock Pact Armor MDR**: Pact Armor now grants binary MDR through `GRANT_RESISTANCE:mystical=true` instead of unsupported `MODIFY_STAT:mdr`. **Recent Updates (2026-02-06)**: - **Starting Equipment**: Arsenal changed from "Choose 2" to "Choose 3" for martial classes. Trade Tools selection added to all classes. - **Progression Feature IDs**: Fixed 12 broken feature ID references across Commander, Monk, Sorcerer, Warlock, Druid, Hunter, and Spellblade progressions. - **Subclass Features**: Added missing subclass feature IDs to Commander, Bard, and Cleric. - **Sorcerer Subclasses**: Corrected 4 subclass feature `levelGained` values from level 1 to level 3 (Celestial Spark, Celestial Appearance, Draconic Spark, Draconic Appearance). --- > _Last updated: 2026-06-23_ > Maintainer: @DC20Clean-Team

markdown:
# DC20Clean - Conditions System

> Purpose: Source-audited condition catalog, condition interaction effects, active condition tracking, and sheet-facing automation.
> Owns: Canonical condition data, condition IDs, condition normalization, active-condition presentation, and supported condition-effect summaries.
> Does not own: Generic effect schemas, encounter turn simulation, automatic target resolution, forced movement, or damage application.
> Authoritative source: `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md`, `docs/migration/conditions-v0105-report.json`, and `src/lib/rulesdata/conditions/conditions.data.ts`.
> Related systems: [Effects](./EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD), [Calculation](./CALCULATION_SYSTEM.MD), [Character Sheet](./CHARACTER_SHEET.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-13

## Source Audit

Conditions are audited against `docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md`.

| File                                                    | Role                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scripts/conditions/dc20-0105-conditions.mjs`           | Parses the v0.10.5 source condition chapter                                                                 |
| `docs/migration/conditions-v0105-report.json`           | Generated flat source audit report with names, source metadata tags, descriptions, provenance, and findings |
| `src/lib/rulesdata/conditions/conditions.data.ts`       | Runtime condition catalog                                                                                   |
| `src/lib/rulesdata/conditions/conditionsSource.test.ts` | Verifies runtime catalog against the generated source report                                                |

Commands:

```bash
npm run conditions:generate:0105
npm run conditions:validate:0105
```

## Catalog Contract

The v0.10.5 universal catalog contains 28 flat condition entries. Source rule
sections such as `stacking`, `overlapping`, `excluded`, and `catalog-only` are
stored only as `sourceTags` metadata on each condition.

`Poisoned` is not a universal v0.10.5 condition. It remains modeled as an effect-specific affliction because individual poisons define their own duration, damage, and riders.

## Source Finding

`Intimidated` appears in the source condition list and is not named in the source "Overlapping Conditions" or "Excluded Conditions" sections. The audit records this with the `catalog-only` source metadata tag.

## Runtime Resolution

`resolveConditionDefinition()` normalizes concrete stacked IDs such as `slowed-2` and `burning-3` to catalog IDs such as `slowed-x` and `burning-x`, preserving the numeric stack value.

`getConditionDefinition()` only returns universal catalog entries by default. Pass `includeEffectSpecific: true` when resolving effect-specific afflictions such as `poisoned`.

Runtime stack controls are driven by `ConditionDefinition.usesStacks`, not by
source metadata tags.

## Effect Interactions

Condition immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities are modeled through the effect system:

- `GRANT_CONDITION_IMMUNITY`
- `GRANT_CONDITION_RESISTANCE`
- `GRANT_CONDITION_VULNERABILITY`

`src/lib/services/conditionAggregator.ts` groups these effects by canonical condition ID. It accepts condition IDs, display names, and concrete stacking IDs.

## Character Sheet Integration

| Surface                  | File                                   | Current behavior                                                              |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Condition reference      | `ConditionsReference.tsx`              | Displays universal condition definitions                                      |
| Standalone reference     | `src/routes/conditions/Conditions.tsx` | Displays the same flat condition catalog outside the character sheet          |
| Condition interactions   | `Conditions.tsx`                       | Displays immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities from aggregated effects |
| Active condition tracker | `ActiveConditionsTracker.tsx`          | Lets users toggle active conditions and set stack values                      |
| Roll badges/modifiers    | `conditionEffectsAnalyzer.ts`          | Applies selected active condition mechanics to sheet rolls and badges         |

Weapon attack details resolve enhancement riders through this catalog. Condition text
is nested under the relevant weapon style; Bleeding also links to the structured
Medicine action rule in `src/lib/rulesdata/coreActions.ts`. This is reference text only
and does not automate Bleeding damage or recovery.

Current automated active-condition effects:

- Attacks: Hindered, Restrained.
- Saves: Immobilized/Restrained on Agility Saves, Weakened on Physical Saves, Disoriented on Mental Saves, Exhaustion on all Saves.
- Checks: Impaired on Physical Checks, Dazed on Mental Checks, Exhaustion on all Checks.
- Movement: Immobilized, Restrained, Slowed, Stunned 4+.

## TODO

- Apply or surface all remaining in-play condition mechanics from the source catalog. # DC20Clean – Database & Storage System

> Purpose: Persistence architecture for characters and DM Tools: hybrid localStorage/Convex storage, schemas, auth, migrations.
> Owns: Persisted data shapes, storage interfaces and adapters, Convex tables, authentication integration, storage normalization, and schema migration.
> Does not own: Game-rule interpretation, derived-stat calculation, feature workflows, or presentation behavior.
> Authoritative source: `src/lib/types/dataContracts.ts`, `src/lib/storage/`, `convex/schema.ts`, and the Convex persistence functions.
> Related systems: [Back Office](./BACK_OFFICE_SYSTEM.MD), [Versioning](./VERSIONING_SYSTEM.MD), [Character Creation](./CHARACTER_CREATION_FLOW.MD), [Character Sheet](./CHARACTER_SHEET.MD), [Campaigns](./CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD), [PDF Export](./PDF_EXPORT_SYSTEM.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-27

---

## 1. Overview

The DC20 Character Creator uses a **hybrid storage model**:

| Storage          | Status           | Use Case                                  |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| **localStorage** | Active (default) | Anonymous users, offline-first            |
| **Convex**       | Active           | Authenticated users, cloud sync, DM Tools |

### 1.1 Data Domains

| Domain               | Tables                                           | Status                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| Characters           | `characters`                                     | Active (Convex + localStorage) |
| DM Tools: Monsters   | `monsters`, `customFeatures`                     | Active (Convex)                |
| DM Tools: Encounters | `encounters`                                     | Active (Convex)                |
| Campaigns            | `campaigns`, `campaignMembers`, `campaignEvents` | Active (Convex only)           |

The storage abstraction layer (`src/lib/storage/`) allows seamless switching between backends.

---

## 2. Data Model

### 2.1 SavedCharacter

The primary data structure for character persistence. Defined in `src/lib/types/dataContracts.ts`.

**Key sections:**

| Section        | Fields                                                                                           | Description                                     |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Identity       | `id`, `finalName`, `finalPlayerName`, `level`                                                    | Core character info                             |
| Class/Ancestry | `classId`, `className`, `ancestry1Id`, `ancestry1Name`, etc.                                     | Build choices                                   |
| Attributes     | `finalMight`, `finalAgility`, `finalCharisma`, `finalIntelligence`                               | Core stats                                      |
| Derived Stats  | `finalHPMax`, `finalSPMax`, `finalMPMax`, `finalPD`, `finalAD`, etc.                             | Calculated values                               |
| Selections     | `selectedTraitIds`, `selectedTraitChoices`, `selectedFeatureChoices`, `skillsData`, `tradesData` | User choices                                    |
| Game State     | `characterState`                                                                                 | Current HP, inventory, notes, etc.              |
| Display Arrays | `resistances?`, `vulnerabilities?`, `senses?`, `combatTraining?`                                 | Calculated display data (v2.2.0+)               |
| Metadata       | `createdAt`, `lastModified`, `schemaVersion`, `rulesVersion`                                     | Timestamps, storage shape, rules interpretation |

### 2.2 Display Arrays (v2.2.0+)

Optional calculated display arrays populated by the calculator for character sheet display:

- **`resistances?`**: `Array<{ type: string; value: number | 'half'; source: string }>` — Damage resistances (e.g., "Fire", "Cold")
- **`vulnerabilities?`**: `Array<{ type: string; value: number | 'half'; source: string }>` — Damage vulnerabilities
- **`senses?`**: `Array<{ type: string; range: number; source: string }>` — Special senses (e.g., "Darkvision", "Tremorsense")
- **`combatTraining?`**: `Array<{ type: string; source: string }>` — Combat training grants (weapons, armor, shields)

These fields are auto-populated from effect system grants (`GRANT_RESISTANCE`, `GRANT_VULNERABILITY`, `GRANT_SENSE`, `GRANT_COMBAT_TRAINING`) and default to empty arrays if missing (migrated automatically).

### 2.3 CharacterState

Runtime state stored within `SavedCharacter.characterState`:

```typescript
interface CharacterState {
	resources: {
		current: {
			currentHP: number;
			currentSP: number;
			currentMP: number;
			currentGritPoints: number;
			currentRestPoints: number;
			tempHP: number;
			actionPointsUsed: number;
			exhaustionLevel: number;
			deathSteps: number;
			isDead: boolean;
		};
	};
	ui: {
		manualDefenseOverrides: { PD?: number; AD?: number; PDR?: number };
		combatToggles?: { isRaging?: boolean };
	};
	inventory: {
		items: InventoryItemData[];
		currency: { gold: number; silver: number; copper: number };
	};
	notes: { playerNotes: string };
	activeConditions?: string[];
	attacks?: AttackData[];
	spells?: SpellData[];
	maneuvers?: ManeuverData[];
}
```

`activeConditions` stores universal condition IDs. Stacking conditions use concrete IDs such as `slowed-2` or `exhaustion-4` in the same string array and normalize back to their catalog IDs at runtime. `characterState.ui.activeConditions` stores older toggle-style UI condition state for compatibility. `defenseOverrides` stores manual precision/area defense overrides from the redesigned sheet.

Attack objects no longer create or type the obsolete `critRange` and `critDamage` keys. The permissive attack storage boundary continues to accept older saved objects containing those keys; current character-sheet code ignores them, so this retirement does not require an in-place migration or schema-version bump.

An attack created through the alternative sheet's Custom weapon source may include an
optional canonical `customWeapon` snapshot. The snapshot is stored inside the existing
permissive `attacks` payload and travels with local, Convex, and JSON character storage.
Older attacks remain valid, and no character schema-version bump is required because the
opaque attack-array contract has not changed.

---

## 3. Storage Architecture

### 3.1 Abstraction Layer

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Application Code                │
│  (CharacterSheetProvider, LoadCharacter)│
└─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                  │
                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│       CharacterStorage Interface        │
│  getAllCharacters(), saveCharacter()    │
└─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                  │
        ┌─────────┴─────────┐
        ▼                   ▼
┌───────────────┐   ┌───────────────┐
│ localStorage  │   │    Convex     │
│   Adapter     │   │   Adapter     │
└───────────────┘   └───────────────┘
```

### 3.2 Interface Definition

```typescript
// src/lib/storage/characterStorage.ts
interface CharacterStorage {
	getAllCharacters(): Promise<SavedCharacter[]>;
	getCharacterById(id: string): Promise<SavedCharacter | null>;
	saveCharacter(character: SavedCharacter): Promise<void>;
	saveAllCharacters(characters: SavedCharacter[]): Promise<void>;
	saveCharacterState(characterId: string, state: CharacterState): Promise<void>;
	deleteCharacter(id: string): Promise<void>;
	backup(): Promise<void>;
	restoreFromBackup(): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### 3.3 Backend Selection

The storage backend is selected via environment variable:

```typescript
// VITE_USE_CONVEX=true → Convex
// VITE_USE_CONVEX=false (or unset) → localStorage
const storage = getDefaultStorage();
```

Local mode does not create a Convex client or mount Convex authentication, so
`VITE_CONVEX_URL` is not required for the default localStorage application.
When `VITE_USE_CONVEX=true`, startup requires `VITE_CONVEX_URL` and fails with a
configuration error if it is missing.

### 3.4 Runtime State Normalization

`normalizeCharacterStateForStorage()` is the shared boundary normalizer for
legacy or partial `SavedCharacter.characterState` data. It fills required
runtime resource fields, UI defaults, inventory currency, notes, and array
surfaces before storage consumers or Convex mutations handle the character.
Convex writes must run character state through this normalizer because table
validators require complete `resources.current` and currency fields, while
older local or cloud records may contain partial nested objects.

`prepareCharacterForSave()` also removes non-persisted JSON export metadata,
character-creation selection inputs, and calculator-only outputs before Convex
writes. Upgrade recalculation and JSON import use object spreads, so those
transient fields can otherwise reach the strict character table validator and
cause `characters:create` to fail even when the saved character fields are
valid.

---

## 4. localStorage Implementation

### 4.1 Storage Key

```
savedCharacters → JSON array of SavedCharacter objects
savedCharacters_backup → Backup copy (for migration safety)
customEquipment → Versioned local Equipage data, including reusable general equipment
```

### 4.2 Key Functions

| Function                  | File              | Purpose                      |
| ------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `getAllSavedCharacters()` | `storageUtils.ts` | Load all characters          |
| `saveAllCharacters()`     | `storageUtils.ts` | Save all characters          |
| `getCharacterById()`      | `storageUtils.ts` | Load single character        |
| `saveCharacter()`         | `storageUtils.ts` | Save/update single character |
| `saveCharacterState()`    | `storageUtils.ts` | Update only game state       |

For an `upgrade-required` character, the sheet passes a resource-filtered state to
`saveCharacterState()`. Only `currentHP`, `tempHP`, `currentMP`, `currentSP`,
`currentRestPoints`, `currentGritPoints`, and `exhaustionLevel` come from the live
sheet. Every other `characterState` field is restored from the last loaded or saved
snapshot before persistence. A resource-save failure never falls back to a full
character save.

Character creation, edit completion, and level-up replacement are single-record
saves. Creation calls `saveCharacter(completedCharacter)` for the new record.
Edit and level-up recalculate the target character and call
`saveCharacter(updatedCharacter)` rather than rewriting the full character list.
This prevents one stale cloud record from blocking a different character's save
under Convex strict validation.

### 4.3 Serialization

- Uses `JSON.stringify()` and `JSON.parse()` internally
- Schema version tracked for migration support
- Automatic migration of legacy formats (e.g., attacks as object → array)

### 4.4 Limitations

- **5-10MB limit** per origin (browser-dependent)
- **No cross-device sync**
- **Data loss risk** if browser data cleared
- **No authentication** - anyone with browser access can see characters

---

## 5. Convex Implementation (Active)

### 5.1 Status

**Active** - Convex is deployed and used for DM Tools and authenticated users.

### 5.2 Schema - Characters

```typescript
// convex/schema.ts
characters: defineTable({
	userId: v.id('users'),
	id: v.string(),
	finalName: v.string(),
	level: v.number()
	// ... all SavedCharacter fields
})
	.index('by_user', ['userId'])
	.index('by_user_and_id', ['userId', 'id'])
	.index('by_user_and_name', ['userId', 'finalName']);
```

### 5.3 Schema - DM Tools: Monsters

```typescript
monsters: defineTable({
  userId: v.id('users'),
  id: v.string(),                    // mon_<uuid>
  name: v.string(),
  level: v.number(),                 // -1 to 10
  tier: v.union(v.literal('standard'), v.literal('apex'), v.literal('legendary')),
  role: v.string(),
  // Stats
  finalHP: v.number(),
  finalPD: v.number(),
  finalAD: v.number(),
  finalAttack: v.number(),
  finalSaveDC: v.number(),
  finalBaseDamage: v.number(),
  // Features & Actions
  featureIds: v.array(v.string()),
  actions: v.array(monsterActionValidator),
  // Sharing & Metadata
  visibility: v.union(...),
  approvalStatus: v.union(...),
  // ...
})
  .index("by_user", ["userId"])
  .index("by_user_and_id", ["userId", "id"])
  .index("by_approval_status", ["approvalStatus"])
  .index("by_user_and_deleted", ["userId", "deletedAt"])

customFeatures: defineTable({
  userId: v.id('users'),
  id: v.string(),                    // feat_<uuid>
  name: v.string(),
  description: v.string(),
  pointCost: v.number(),             // 1-5
  // Sharing fields...
})
  .index("by_user", ["userId"])
  .index("by_approval_status", ["approvalStatus"])
```

### 5.4 Schema - DM Tools: Encounters

```typescript
encounters: defineTable({
  userId: v.id('users'),
  id: v.string(),                    // enc_<uuid>
  name: v.string(),
  party: partyConfigValidator,       // { size, averageLevel }
  difficulty: v.union(v.literal('trivial'), ...),
  // Budget
  baseBudget: v.number(),
  adjustedBudget: v.number(),
  spentBudget: v.number(),
  remainingBudget: v.number(),
  // Monster Slots
  monsters: v.array(encounterMonsterSlotValidator),
  // Sharing & Metadata
  visibility: v.union(...),
  approvalStatus: v.union(...),
  // ...
})
  .index("by_user", ["userId"])
  .index("by_user_and_id", ["userId", "id"])
  .index("by_approval_status", ["approvalStatus"])
  .index("by_user_and_deleted", ["userId", "deletedAt"])
```

### 5.5 Authentication

- **Google OAuth** via Convex Auth
- User ID linked to all records
- Data only visible to owner (except approved homebrew)
- `users.getCurrentUser` returns the stable string `userId`, optional display name,
  and the user document `_creationTime` as `createdAt`. Consumers preserve
  `undefined` while the query resolves and use `null` for a resolved signed-out state.
- Convex authentication is mounted only when `VITE_USE_CONVEX=true`; local mode
  uses an unauthenticated app-auth context, keeps cloud-only routes hidden, and
  renders a disabled `Sign In` affordance so the top-right toolbar does not look
  like a language-only control.

### 5.6 Auth UI & Access Control

**Components** (`src/components/auth/`):

| Component              | Purpose                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `AuthStatus`           | Sign in button / user menu in header      |
| `SignIn`               | OAuth sign-in dialog with feature context |
| `AuthGuard`            | Route protection wrapper                  |
| `useIsAuthenticated()` | Hook to check auth state                  |

**Access Control by Feature**:

| Feature                                                     | Auth Required | Notes                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Character Creation                                          | No            | Saves to localStorage without auth   |
| Character Creation → Save                                   | **Prompted**  | Auth dialog when clicking "Complete" |
| Load Character                                              | No            | Loads from localStorage              |
| DM Tools (Laboratory, War Room)                             | **Yes**       | Menu items hidden until signed in    |
| Reference Tools (Spellbook, Conditions, Equipage, Rulebook) | No            | Public access                        |

│  User clicks "Complete" on final step                       │

Key implementation: `src/routes/character-creation/CharacterCreation.tsx`

- `pendingSave` state tracks when waiting for auth
- `useEffect` auto-triggers save when auth completes
- No duplicate saves or manual re-click needed

### 5.7 Benefits

- **Cloud sync** across devices
- **Data safety** - server-side backups
- **Scalability** - no localStorage limits
- **User accounts** - content ownership
- **Sharing** - homebrew library for community content

## 6. Migration & Compatibility

Internal versioning policy is defined in `docs/systems/VERSIONING_SYSTEM.MD`. This
storage system owns `schemaVersion` persistence and participates in `rulesVersion`
compatibility, but it must not conflate those lanes.

### 6.1 Schema Versioning

```typescript
const CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = '2.2.0';

// Each character stores its version
character.schemaVersion = CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION;
```

**Current Version**: `2.2.0` (as of 2026-06-01)

`schemaVersion` is only the storage-shape version. It must not be used to infer which DC20 rules text a character was built under. Numeric legacy values such as `2` are normalized to semver strings during load/save.

**Version History**:

- `2.0.0`: Initial schema
- `2.1.0`: Added `selectedFeatureChoices`, migrated `selectedTalents` from array to count-based record
- `2.2.0`: Added optional display arrays (`resistances`, `vulnerabilities`, `senses`, `combatTraining`)

### 6.2 Rules Versioning

```typescript
const CURRENT_RULES_VERSION = 'dc20-0.10.5';

// Missing rulesVersion is inferred as the legacy v0.10 ruleset.
character.rulesVersion ?? 'dc20-0.10';
```

`rulesVersion` is the rules interpretation fence. It is additive and is preserved on load, import, save, Convex normalization, draft state, character sheet auto-save, and PDF export routing. New characters are saved as `dc20-0.10.5`; missing or explicit `dc20-0.10` characters are legacy and classify as `upgrade-required` under the current runtime.

Compatibility states are computed at runtime:

| State              | Load | Sheet render | Edit / level up | Auto-save                                       | PDF export                      |
| ------------------ | ---- | ------------ | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `editable`         | Yes  | Yes          | Yes             | Full character save with recalculation          | Yes                             |
| `upgrade-required` | Yes  | Yes          | Resources only  | Seven current resource fields; no recalculation | Best-effort stored-value export |
| `view-only`        | Yes  | Best effort  | Blocked         | Disabled                                        | Best-effort stored-value export |

#### Explicit v0.10 to Current-Version Copy

`LoadCharacter.tsx` exposes an update-to-current-version action for legacy characters. The action is planned
and applied by `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/characterUpgrade.ts`:

1. Inspect every persisted feature, trait, talent, spell, and maneuver selection through the
   versioned alias catalog.
2. Show automatic renames, reworked selections, deprecated removals, and unresolved blockers
   before writing data.
3. Refuse copy creation when an identity is ambiguous or the source rules version is unsupported.
4. Create a new current-rules copy with lineage metadata (`rulesUpgradeSourceId`,
   `rulesUpgradeSourceVersion`, `rulesUpgradedAt`) while leaving the legacy source record
   locked and unchanged.
5. Rewrite approved aliases, explicitly map listed reworks, remove listed deprecated selections
   in the new copy, and set that copy to `dc20-0.10.5`.
6. Mark the new copy `rulesUpgradeStatus: "needs-review"` for any risky result: removed
   choices, reworked choices, unresolved validation, or failed recalculation.

Migration never mutates the old instance's build or sheet content. The legacy source remains view/export/delete plus live-resource management only. The new copy preserves stored game state,
notes, inventory, and resources where possible; derived values are interpreted and recalculated
by the normal v0.10.5 sheet/editor pipeline after migration.

If a legacy character already has a current-rules copy, the default UI action opens that copy.
Users can explicitly create another copy from a secondary action.

PDF export always reads stored `SavedCharacter` values. It does not run the current calculator
during export for either legacy or current characters.

### 6.3 Auto-Migration

When loading characters, local storage deserialization automatically normalizes:

1. Adds missing fields with defaults
2. Converts legacy formats (object → array)
3. Updates schema version
4. Applies the same normalization to pasted character JSON import before saving

This is read-time normalization. It becomes durable when the normalized character is later saved. The legacy attacks object-map migration is the only localStorage migration currently persisted immediately on single-character lookup.

**Migration to v2.2.0**: Characters migrating from v2.1.0 or earlier receive empty/default-compatible display fields (`resistances`, `vulnerabilities`, `senses`, `combatTraining`) when loaded and are persisted on the next full save.

Imported older JSON is normalized through the same deserializer before duplicate-ID handling and save, so legacy stringified arrays, missing `rulesVersion`, and older talent shapes follow the same compatibility path as existing localStorage records.

### 6.4 localStorage → Convex Migration

**Not automatic** - users must:

1. Export characters to JSON (existing feature)
2. Sign in to Convex
3. Import characters (existing feature)

### 6.5 Convex Schema Update Workflow

When validators or table definitions change in `convex/`:

1. Run `npx convex dev --once`
2. Commit schema/function changes together with `convex/_generated/*`
3. Roll out frontend code that consumes the updated generated API

The Convex adapter omits empty optional root records for fields introduced in a
newer frontend schema when that preserves compatibility with a stale deployed
Convex table validator. Non-empty records are still sent and require the Convex
backend schema to be deployed.

import { getDefaultStorage } from '@/lib/storage';

## 9. Campaign Tables

See `docs/systems/CAMPAIGN_SYSTEM.MD` for full schema details, permission model, and frontend architecture.

### 9.1 `campaigns`

| Field          | Type          | Notes                                |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `userId`       | `Id<'users'>` | Creator / DM                         |
| `id`           | `string`      | App-generated id, e.g. `camp_<uuid>` |
| `code`         | `string`      | 6-char alphanumeric join code        |
| `name`         | `string`      |                                      |
| `description`  | `string?`     |                                      |
| `createdAt`    | `string`      | ISO timestamp                        |
| `lastModified` | `string`      | ISO timestamp                        |
| `deletedAt`    | `string?`     | Soft-delete                          |

Indexes: `by_user` (userId), `by_app_id` (id — note: `by_id` is Convex-reserved), `by_code` (code).

### 9.2 `campaignMembers`

| Field                   | Type                          | Notes                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `campaignId`            | `Id<'campaigns'>`             |                                                           |
| `userId`                | `Id<'users'>`                 |                                                           |
| `role`                  | `'dm' \| 'co_dm' \| 'player'` |                                                           |
| `sharedCharacterIds`    | `string[]`                    | Compatibility copy of app-level character IDs             |
| `sharedCharacterDocIds` | `Id<'characters'>[]?`         | Authoritative connected records; optional for legacy rows |
| `displayName`           | `string?`                     | Captured at join time                                     |
| `joinedAt`              | `string`                      | ISO timestamp                                             |
| `deletedAt`             | `string?`                     | Soft-delete                                               |

Indexes: `by_campaign` (campaignId), `by_user` (userId), `by_campaign_and_user` (campaignId, userId).

When `sharedCharacterDocIds` exists, campaign reads treat it as authoritative. Rows without it resolve `sharedCharacterIds` only within the member owner's characters and are lazily upgraded on reconnect. The optional field is an additive Convex table migration; it does not change the saved-character schema.

### 9.3 `campaignEvents`

| Field         | Type              | Notes                                 |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `campaignId`  | `Id<'campaigns'>` |                                       |
| `type`        | `string`          | e.g. `well_bloodied`, `member_joined` |
| `actorUserId` | `Id<'users'>`     |                                       |
| `characterId` | `string?`         | App-level character id                |
