markdown:
# DC20Clean - Testing System

> Purpose: Central testing policy for source audits, rules data, calculator behavior, UI components, and Playwright E2E flows.
> Owns: Test-layer policy, test placement, validation commands, E2E standards, agentic QA conventions, and repository-wide quality gates.
> Does not own: Subsystem behavior, business acceptance semantics, source rules content, or feature-specific ownership boundaries.
> Authoritative source: `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`, `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`, `e2e/`, and colocated test files.
> Related systems: Every behavior-specific system doc defines what must be proven; this document defines where and how to prove it.
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-21

---

## 1. Test Layers

| Layer                    | Tooling                   | Location                                            | Purpose                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source audits            | Node scripts              | `scripts/*/dc20-0105-*.mjs`, `scripts/classes/*.ts` | Compare runtime rules data to the v0.10.5 source artifact and generated reports          |
| Rules data tests         | Vitest                    | `src/lib/rulesdata/**/*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`       | Validate schemas, IDs, source drift, generated catalogs, and feature references          |
| Calculator tests         | Vitest                    | `src/lib/services/**/*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`        | Validate exact mechanical outcomes from selected effects and character inputs            |
| UI logic/component tests | Vitest + Testing Library  | `src/routes/**/*.test.tsx`, `*.logic.test.ts`       | Validate local UI state, reducers, step gating, and component rendering                  |
| Convex domain tests      | Vitest + `convex-test`    | `convex/**/*.test.ts`                               | Validate authenticated backend lifecycles against isolated in-memory Convex state        |
| Acceptance features      | Gherkin                   | `e2e/features/*.feature`                            | Define readable cross-surface lifecycle contracts mapped to executable lower-layer tests |
| E2E tests                | Playwright                | `e2e/*.e2e.spec.ts`                                 | Validate representative user journeys, persistence, import/export, and sheet surfaces    |
| Agentic browser QA       | Playwright + repo scripts | `e2e/agentic/*`, `scripts/e2e/*`                    | Run declarative character recipes, collect artifacts, and compare results to oracles     |

Use the lowest layer that can prove the behavior. Do not move combinatorial rules math into E2E when a deterministic calculator test can prove it faster and with better failure messages.

---

## 2. Commands

Primary gates:

```bash
npm run test:unit -- --project server --run <focused files>
npm run test:unit -- --project convex --run <focused Convex files>
npm run test:e2e -- --project=desktop <focused e2e spec>
git diff --check
```

System audit gates:

```bash
npm run spells:validate:0105
npm run martials:validate:0105
npm run ancestries:validate:0105
npm run background:validate:0105
npm run background:names:validate:0105
npm run background:traits:validate:0105
npm run conditions:validate:0105
npm run classes:validate:0105
npm run classes:effects:validate
npm run classes:audit:validate
npm run leveling:review:validate:0105
```

Full local gates:

```bash
npm run test:unit -- --run
npm run test:e2e
```

All general E2E commands use `e2e/test-character-current.json`, currently a
canonical `dc20-0.10.5` character generated through the live creation flow.
`E2E_FIXTURE` may override it only for a deliberate compatibility investigation;
committed legacy-version coverage must construct or name its fixture inside the
explicit upgrade or compatibility spec.

Vitest uses `client` (browser), `server` (Node), and `convex` (Edge runtime) projects. Tests that stub `import.meta.env` or process-backed environment state must stay in the server project and be excluded from the browser project. Convex function tests use `convex-test` and authenticate with `t.withIdentity`.
The PostHog SDK adapter test is server-only; analytics privacy and React lifecycle tests also run in the browser project.
Flag tests must prove PostHog starts without a consent choice when the legal/consent flow is off, while its routes, links, and controls are hidden. With the flow on, consent tests prove no PostHog initialization before a valid analytics choice, cancellation of queued captures after withdrawal, and resume on reacceptance. Browser checks must confirm public signed-out legal access and both languages only with that flag on, plus no Userback request before an explicit feedback action.

Agentic browser QA gates:

```bash
npm run e2e:agentic:smoke
npm run e2e:agentic
npm run e2e:agentic:generate
npm run e2e:agentic:summarize
```

Known environment note: browser/E2E failures can be environment-driven when Playwright browsers are missing. For rules migration slices, focused server tests plus source-audit validators are the stronger first signal.

Responsive UI changes must verify the shared boundary pairs rather than arbitrary device names:

1. Compact/tablet: 767px and 768px.
2. Tablet/desktop: 1199px and 1200px.
3. Include at least one narrow phone width, currently 390px, and assert `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth`.
4. Prefer component-width assertions and visible controls over screenshot-only checks.

---

## 3. Coverage Contract

For any rules behavior change, add or verify coverage in this order:

1. Source audit: generated report is current when source-derived data changes.
2. Rules data test: schema, IDs, and references are valid.
3. Calculator test: exact mechanical result is asserted from a minimal character.
4. UI/component test: required display or interaction state is asserted without a full browser flow.
5. E2E test: only when the behavior must prove wizard flow, persistence, import/load, sheet visibility, or cross-page behavior.

E2E should test user-facing acceptance cases, not every rule permutation.

Agentic browser QA is the escalation layer for broad permutation coverage. It
should generate and execute bounded recipes, not replace lower-level source,
rules-data, or calculator tests.

### 3.1 Cross-Surface Lifecycle Features

For a lifecycle that spans UI presentations, backend records, permissions, and subscriptions:

1. Write the complete readable contract in `e2e/features/*.feature`.
2. Back deterministic domain behavior with executable tests at the lowest sufficient layer.
3. Keep scenario names aligned between the feature and executable tests.
4. Add focused component or Playwright coverage for routing and presentation-specific wiring.
5. Do not count a `.feature` file alone as regression protection.

Legacy resource-only compatibility is covered by the versioning classifier tests and
`CharacterSheetProvider.compatibility.test.tsx`. Coverage must prove both sides of the
boundary: the seven permitted live values persist without calculation, while attempted
inventory, notes, attacks, and non-permitted resource-state changes remain unchanged.
Shared Playwright fixtures for structural sheet editing must declare the current
`rulesVersion` and be generated through the current character-creation flow. Legacy
fixtures belong in explicit compatibility or upgrade scenarios and must not be relabeled.

### 3.2 Rules Acceptance Features

1. Use a readable Gherkin scenario when several progression sources combine into one expected character result.
2. Back the scenario with a focused rules-data or calculator test using the same named choices and exact totals.
3. `e2e/features/wizard-level-5-progression.feature` maps to `src/lib/services/dc20v0105ProgressionResources.test.ts`.

### 3.3 Alternative Character Sheet Integration TODO

Add a current-rules character-page suite that proves presentation and calculations stay
connected across the shared provider, calculator, and alternative sheet:

1. Magic context:
   1. a noncaster hides Mana, Mana Spend Limit, and Spells;
   2. an AP-only caster shows Spells without showing Mana or Mana Spend Limit;
   3. a Mana caster shows Mana, Mana Spend Limit, and Spells;
   4. the Meta Magic exemption appears only for a character that owns the canonical feature,
      including a multiclass grant.
2. Combat feature modes:
   1. Rage appears only for a character that owns the canonical feature;
   2. activating and deactivating Rage updates the shared condition state and survives the
      intended sheet-state lifecycle.
3. Derived combat results:
   1. active Rage applies the PD penalty and restores PD when deactivated;
   2. its damage bonus applies to Unarmed Strikes and melee weapons, but not ranged weapons;
   3. its Might Save ADV source is visible and participates in normal ADV/DisADV cancellation.

The focused `Spells.test.tsx` component coverage is complete for the alternative
picker no-blank-row, next-slot eligibility, full-catalog ordering, confirmation flow,
search, school filtering, and compact catalog-toolbar composition. It also proves the
alternative-only focused casting modal, MSL control guard, exact Mana deduction,
campaign callback, and close-on-confirm behavior. `spellCastSpend.test.ts` isolates
fixed, repeatable, variable, alternative-resource, and prerequisite cost calculation.
`e2e/22-alternative-spell-cast.e2e.spec.ts` completes the browser path through the
visible Mana card. `Attacks.test.tsx`
proves weapon search and melee/ranged filtering. Both source-switching pickers preserve
their active search and filter. It also proves the separate v0.10.5 five-panel
custom-weapon builder creates a populated attack with an embedded canonical snapshot,
exposes reskinned styles across weapon types, and returns to the unchanged picker state
when cancelled. It also proves contextual guidance moves with the active build-sheet
section instead of remaining visible across stages, and that damage type has its own
2.5 stage between style and properties. `Maneuvers.test.tsx` proves the
alternative picker creates complete catalog data without a blank row and excludes
already-known maneuvers, including name search and type filtering. `Inventory.test.tsx`
proves alternative inventory creation is mutation-free until confirmation, with

## 7. E2E Standards

- Prefer `data-testid` selectors for stable app-owned controls.
- For Userback/UI feedback changes, validate with `npm run build` and a browser request check: no Userback script loads before the person chooses the footer action and confirms its disclosure; keep app-supplied payloads limited to compact metadata.
- Recipe-style E2E tests should be written as named user actions and visible assertions. They may use Playwright as the executor, but the test should read as a deterministic user journey rather than DOM plumbing.
- Add lightweight semantic hooks (`data-testid`, `data-step-id`, `aria-current`) for agent/browser discovery when the visible control is part of a cross-page flow.
- Assert explicit visible state or saved localStorage state after each meaningful action.
- Cross-page persistence E2E tests should attach targeted diagnostics on failure:
  current URL, relevant console/page errors, and a compact saved-character
  snapshot before/after the action under test.
- Avoid screenshot-only success criteria.
- Keep one spec focused on one user story.
- Do not use broad text selectors when the same string can appear in hidden options, flavor text, or unrelated cards.
- If a behavior is calculated but not visibly rendered, add a UI TODO or component test instead of pretending E2E covered it.

## 8. Agentic Browser QA

Goal: let a local or cloud runner create characters through the real UI, collect
diagnostic artifacts, and compare the result against deterministic calculator
expectations.

This is an in-repo testing layer, not an external service.

### 8.1 Ownership

Implemented first-slice files:

1. `e2e/agentic/recipes/*.ts`
   1. Declarative character-creation recipes.
   2. Recipes specify intended choices by stable IDs, not visible copy.
   3. Recipes may include expected high-level assertions such as class, level,
      resources, known spells, known maneuvers, senses, defenses, and sheet/export
      visibility.
2. `e2e/agentic/support/recipeExecutor.ts`
   1. Executes recipes through Playwright as user-visible actions.
   2. Uses semantic hooks first and visible roles second.
3. `e2e/agentic/support/runLogger.ts`
   1. Captures console logs, page errors, failed requests, current URL,
      screenshots on failure, selected choices, saved character JSON, and
      downloaded JSON/PDF metadata when relevant.
   2. Writes artifacts under `test-results/agentic/<run-id>/`.
4. `e2e/agentic/support/oracles.ts`
   1. Calls app calculator/source data directly.
   2. Builds a persisted-data expectation report from the recipe and saved
      character.
   3. Compares deterministic calculator outputs and sheet-visible values.
5. `scripts/e2e/generateCharacterRecipes.ts`
   1. Generates bounded recipe sets from current rules data.
   2. Supports smoke, class-by-class, high-risk, and pairwise coverage modes.
6. `scripts/e2e/summarizeAgenticRuns.ts`
   1. Produces readable JSON/Markdown summaries from run artifacts.

Current inventory:

1. `e2e/agentic/recipes/spellbladeHybridSmoke.ts`
   1. Smoke recipe for a Spellblade/Human hybrid character.
   2. Covers conditional spell and maneuver steps.
   3. Pins selected spells and maneuvers by catalog ID.
   4. Defines the expected saved-character slice for identity, final stats,
      traits, skills, trades, languages, combat training, spells, and maneuvers.
2. `e2e/agentic/recipes/humanBarbarianCanonical.ts`
   1. Canonical level-1 Human Barbarian recipe based on the manual QA path.
   2. Covers Human ancestry spend, point-buy attributes, Background skill/trade/language budgets, Maneuver learning, saved-character oracle checks, and sheet opening.
   3. Mirrors the deterministic recipe in `e2e/14-character-creation-flow.e2e.spec.ts`.
3. `e2e/agentic/recipes/clericCanonical.ts`
   1. Canonical level-3 Cleric recipe.
   2. Covers class feature choices, subclass selection, talent selection,
      cross-path Martial investment, dual ancestry, ancestry calc traits,
      background conversions, Skill/Trade mastery cap exceptions, spells, and
      maneuvers.
   3. Asserts exact final stats, selected feature choices, selected talents,
      path allocations, Darkvision range, saved background selections, selected
      spells, selected maneuvers, and combat training.
4. `e2e/agentic/agentic-character-creation.e2e.spec.ts`
   1. Runs smoke recipes through Playwright.
   2. Captures saved character JSON and run artifacts.
   3. Writes `saved-expectation-report.json`.
   4. Opens the saved character sheet after oracle validation, or continues if
      completion already navigated directly to the sheet.
   5. Checks recipe-defined sheet-visible text.
5. `scripts/e2e/calculateAgenticOracle.ts`
   1. Runs under `vite-node`.
   2. Recalculates saved characters through `calculateCharacterWithBreakdowns`.
   3. Reports stat and selection mismatches.

Agentic gate policy:

1. Automated deterministic checks should stay cheap enough to run on every local change and PR: focused Vitest, focused deterministic Playwright specs, and `git diff --check`.
2. Agentic browser QA remains opt-in for ordinary PRs and is required for release
   candidates and changes to creation budgets, step gating, or cross-page persistence.
3. Candidate agentic triggers: nightly runs, release candidates, broad character-creation changes, rules-data migrations, Background/Class/Ancestry budget changes, and failures that only appear through full UI persistence.
4. Nightly/release runs retain artifacts for failed recipes; local focused runs retain
   only failure artifacts. Environment failures do not block a release until reproduced
   with the deterministic focused Playwright spec.

### 8.2 UI Agent Contract

The UI should expose stable, machine-readable hooks for creation, sheet, import,
export, and upgrade flows.

Required hook patterns:

1. Flow and step state:
   1. `data-flow-id`
   2. `data-step-id`
   3. `aria-current="step"`
   4. `aria-disabled`
2. Selectable options:
   1. `data-option-id`
   2. `data-class-id`
   3. `data-ancestry-id`
   4. `data-trait-id`
   5. `data-feature-id`
   6. `data-spell-id`
   7. `data-maneuver-id`
   8. `data-talent-id`
3. Inputs and controls:
   1. `data-field-id`
   2. `aria-invalid`
   3. `data-action-id`
4. Budgets and validation:
   1. `data-budget-id`
   2. `data-budget-remaining`
   3. `data-validation-code`

Visible text remains for humans. Agentic tests should prefer stable IDs and
accessibility state over visible prose.

### 8.3 Optional Dev/Test Snapshot

In dev/test only, the app may expose a read-only browser snapshot:

```ts
window.__DC20_AGENT_STATE__;
```

Suggested contents:

1. route
2. current flow ID
3. current step ID
4. completed step IDs
5. selected option IDs
6. budget summaries
7. calculator summary
8. validation errors with codes
9. available actions/options

The snapshot is diagnostic. Recipes must still execute through UI actions so the
flow remains user-realistic.

### 8.4 Oracle Rules

1. Expected rules math must come from app calculator/source-data code.
2. Expected UI visibility should come from recipe assertions.
3. Expected export data should compare against the saved character JSON and PDF
   transformer output, not against screenshots.
4. Do not use snapshots as a substitute for checking important derived values.

### 8.5 Failure Classification

Agentic runs should classify failures into:

1. selector or semantic-hook gap
2. UI flow regression
3. calculator mismatch
4. persistence mismatch
5. export mismatch
6. rules-data/catalog gap
7. environment/tooling failure

The first implementation should be self-diagnosing, not self-healing. A
self-healing layer may later propose patches or selector additions, but it must
not silently rewrite selectors, recipes, or expected values.

### 8.6 First Implementation Slice

Status: implemented.

1. `runLogger` captures browser logs, page errors, failed requests, screenshots on

2. Declarative recipe types live in `e2e/agentic/recipes/types.ts`.

## 9. When To Add Tests

Add focused tests when changing:

- Effect schema or calculator effect handling.
- Source-generated data or audit scripts.
- Character creation step gating or validation.
- Character sheet display of calculated values.
- Persistence, version upgrade, import/export, or PDF output.
- Analytics identity, event registration, or privacy filtering. Cover pure sanitizers and the SDK adapter in server tests, React lifecycle ordering in a client test, Convex identity shape in a Convex test, and the deployed ingestion boundary with a privacy-safe production event.
- Any rules behavior where a user can make a selection and expect derived values to change.
- Agentic browser recipes or UI agent hooks.

Do not modify existing tests just to make a failing test pass unless the expected behavior has been re-reviewed against source/system docs.

Write unit tests. --- ## 5 Troubleshooting FAQ 🤖 | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Trait not visible / loaded | Not added to `ancestries/traits.ts` or `id` mismatch | Verify entry and `id` format | | Unit test `rulesdata.spec.ts` fails | Missing required fields or malformed `effects` | Ensure `id`, `name`, `cost`, and `effects[]` are present | | Stats not updating for new numeric effect | `target` not recognized in calculator | Map `target` in `createStatBreakdown` or associated aggregators (e.g., `finalAttributePoints`) | | Choice prompt not appearing in UI | `effect.userChoice` missing or unresolved | Add `userChoice`; ensure `resolveEffectChoices` supports target | | Vite import error for traits | Import path typo | Use `ancestries/traits` | --- ## 6 Testing 🧪 ### 6.1 Test Suite **Location**: `src/lib/rulesdata/ancestries/ancestries.test.ts` **Coverage**: Comprehensive tests (including Phase 8c tests) validating all trait data. #### Test Categories **Trait Data Structure** - ✅ Trait data loads successfully (178 `traitsData` entries; 180 source traits including Fallen/Redeemed variant traits) - ✅ Required fields present (`id`, `name`, `description`, `cost`, `effects`) - ✅ Unique trait IDs (no duplicates) - ✅ Valid cost values (numeric) - ✅ Non-empty effects arrays **ID Format & Naming** - ✅ `ancestry_trait` naming convention followed - ✅ Trait ID prefixes match ancestry IDs (e.g., `human_*`, `elf_*`) **Trait-to-Ancestry Relationships** - ✅ Zero orphaned traits (all traits referenced by at least one ancestry) - ✅ All trait references resolve to existing traits - ✅ No duplicates in trait lists **Effect Validation** - ✅ Only valid effect types used (see `EFFECT_SYSTEM.MD`) - ✅ Valid target values for `MODIFY_STAT` effects - ✅ Numeric values for numeric effect types - ✅ Proper `userChoice` structure for choice-based effects - ✅ **All effects have required `target` field** (not `count` or `options`) **Cost & Budget** - ✅ Valid costs for negative traits (negative values, `isNegative: true`) - ✅ Consistent cost structure across all traits - ✅ Default trait costs sum correctly for each ancestry **Statistics** - 11 core ancestries defined - 178 `traitsData` entries defined - 180 source traits tracked in `docs/migration/ancestries-v0105-report.json` including Fallen/Redeemed variant traits - Effect type distribution tracked - Cost distribution tracked - Core runtime trait names and costs are compared against the generated v0.10.5 source report ### 6.2 Running Tests ```bash # Run ancestry & trait tests npm run test:unit -- ancestries.test.ts # With detailed output npm run test:unit -- ancestries.test.ts --reporter=verbose # Watch mode (for development) npm run test:unit -- ancestries.test.ts --watch ``` ### 6.3 Test-Driven Data Quality The test suite enforces strict data quality: - **No orphaned traits**: Every trait must be used by at least one ancestry - **Strict schema**: All effects must have `type`, `target`, and `value` - **Naming conventions**: Trait IDs must follow `ancestry_trait` pattern - **Required fields**: Missing `id`, `name`, `cost`, or `effects` fails tests - **Valid references**: All trait IDs in ancestry lists must exist ### 6.4 When Tests Fail | Test Failure | Fix | | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | "should have unique trait IDs" | Remove duplicate trait definition | | "should reference only existing traits" | Fix typo in trait ID or create missing trait | | "should not have orphaned traits" | Add trait to an ancestry's trait list or remove unused trait | | "should have valid effect structure" | Add `target` field to effect (not `count` or inline `options`) | | "should follow ancestry_trait naming" | Rename trait ID to match `ancestry_trait` pattern | --- ## 7 Trait Prerequisite Chains Traits with prerequisites require the base trait to be selected before the enhanced trait becomes available. The UI enforces these prerequisites and provides visual feedback when requirements are not met. ### 7.1 Complete Prerequisite Map | Base Trait | Enhanced Traits (require base) | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Beastborn** | | | Climb Speed | Spider Climb | | Glide Speed | Limited Flight | | Limited Flight | Flyby, Full Flight | | Thick-Skinned | Shell | | Natural Weapon | Extended Natural Weapon, Ranged Natural Weapon, Natural Weapon Style, Rending Natural Weapon, Retractable Natural Weapon, Venomous Natural Weapon | | Additional Limb | Capable Limb | | **Dragonborn** | | | Draconic Breath Weapon | Concussive Breath, Death's Breath, Improved Draconic Breath | | **Fiendborn** | | | Darkvision | Superior Darkvision | | **Giantborn** | | | Giant's Resolve | Giant's Fortitude | ### 7.2 Multi-Level Chains Some traits form chains of multiple levels: ``` Glide Speed → Limited Flight → Flyby Glide Speed → Limited Flight → Full Flight ``` ### 7.3 UI Behavior When a prerequisite is not met: - Enhanced trait displays "Requires: [Base Trait Name]" in amber text - Checkbox is disabled and cursor shows not-allowed - Visual styling indicates unavailability (opacity reduced) When deselecting a base trait: - All dependent enhanced traits are automatically deselected (cascade) - This prevents orphaned selections ### 7.4 Data Schema Prerequisites are defined using the `requirements` field (preferred) or the legacy `prerequisites` array: #### Preferred: `requirements` Object The `requirements` field provides structured prerequisite logic: ```typescript { id: 'beastborn_enhanced_flight', name: 'Enhanced Flight', description: '...', cost: 2, requirements: { hasTrait: ['beastborn_winged_arms', 'beastborn_webbed_hands'], // Requires ANY of these (OR logic) hasAllTraits: ['beastborn_winged_arms', 'beastborn_strong_wings'], // Requires ALL of these (AND logic) prohibitsTraits: ['beastborn_grounded'] // Cannot be taken if any of these are selected }, effects: [...] } ``` **Field Descriptions:** - `requirements.hasTrait: string[]` — Trait requires any ONE of the listed traits (OR logic). This supersedes the simple `prerequisites` array for "any-of" scenarios. - `requirements.hasAllTraits: string[]` — Trait requires ALL listed traits to be selected (AND logic). - `requirements.prohibitsTraits: string[]` — Trait cannot be taken if any of these traits are selected. #### Legacy: `prerequisites` Array The `prerequisites` field is still supported for simple single-trait requirements: ```typescript { id: 'beastborn_spider_climb', name: 'Spider Climb', description: '...', cost: 1, prerequisites: ['beastborn_climb_speed'], // Simple array: requires this trait effects: [...] } ``` **Migration Note:** New traits should use `requirements.hasTrait` for "any-of" scenarios instead of `prerequisites`. At runtime, every remaining legacy `prerequisites` array is populated into `requirements.hasAllTraits`. Explicit structured requirements remain authoritative for any-of and prohibition semantics. A data test prevents prerequisite chains from escaping the structured contract. --- ## 8 Future Evolution - Effect Processor unification may centralize trait effect resolution across ancestries and classes. - Schema-driven editors may auto-render trait forms from `Trait` and `Effect` metadata. - Integration tests may validate that trait effects correctly modify character stats in the calculator. ## 9 DC20 v0.10.5 Notes - Core trait runtime scope is limited to the 11 core v0.10.5 ancestries. Magazine/non-core traits for Gremlin, Goblin, Terraborn, Shadowborn, and Psyborn are not exported in `traitsData`. - `npm run ancestries:generate:0105` parses the source ancestry chapter and writes `docs/migration/ancestries-v0105-report.json`. - `npm run ancestries:validate:0105` fails if that report is stale. - `ancestries.test.ts` compares runtime core trait names and point costs against the generated source report. Runtime descriptions/effects remain human-reviewed. - `beastborn_hazardous_hide` remains the stable ID for Hazardous Hide. It is a current v0.10.5 Beastborn Body trait, not an alias or resurrected saved-data rewrite. - `beastborn_additional_limb` now reflects the v0.10.5 1 Space limb, object handling, push/pull/grapple, and no Weapon/Shield/Spell Focus/Somatic use limitations. - `beastborn_capable_limb` costs 2 points and upgrades an Additional Limb to use Weapons, Shields, Spell Focuses, and Somatic Components. Its prerequisite remains `beastborn_additional_limb`. - `beastborn_natural_weapon_style` is the current v0.10.5 Natural Weapon trait. The stale `beastborn_natural_weapon_passive` record was removed. - `beastborn_natural_weapon` derives a read-only Unarmed Strike on the character sheet. Its unresolved Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing choice is presented as `B/P/S`; this display behavior does not add an attack to persisted character state. - Current trait data uses `GRANT_SPELL` for every spell grant. Fiendish Aura grants Sorcery through that current effect and uses Spell terminology; `GRANT_CANTRIP` remains compatibility-only outside the current trait catalog. --- > Last updated: 2026-06-19 > Maintainer: @DC20Clean-Team

# DC20Clean – Internal Versioning System

> Purpose: Canonical policy for schema, rules, PDF, and system-source versioning.
> Owns: Version-lane definitions, rules-version normalization, compatibility classification, upgrade routing, schema-version policy, PDF-version routing policy, and source-version metadata requirements.
> Does not own: Subsystem rules content, storage implementation details, PDF field mapping, or feature-specific migration UI.
> Authoritative source: `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/`, `src/lib/types/schemaVersion.ts`, and the version constants owned by individual subsystems.
> Related systems: [Database](./DATABASE_SYSTEM.MD), [PDF Export](./PDF_EXPORT_SYSTEM.MD), [Character Creation](./CHARACTER_CREATION_FLOW.MD), [Project Technical Overview](./PROJECT_TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.MD).
> Status: Active
> Last Updated: 2026-09-19

---

## 1. Version Types

DC20Clean uses separate version lanes. Do not collapse them into one field.

| Lane                 | Field / Constant                          | Meaning                                          | Current         |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------- |
| App/package          | `package.json.version`                    | Release/package version of the app itself        | `0.10.5`        |
| Storage schema       | `schemaVersion`, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Shape of saved character data                    | `2.2.0`         |
| Rules interpretation | `rulesVersion`, `CURRENT_RULES_VERSION`   | DC20 ruleset used to interpret saved choices     | `dc20-0.10.5`   |
| PDF target           | `PdfVersion`, field maps                  | Fillable PDF template/field-map target           | `0.10`          |
| System source        | system constants/docs                     | Source artifact and section used for a subsystem | system-specific |

## 2. Canonical Formats

- Rules versions use the `dc20-<version>` form, for example `dc20-0.10.5`.
- Legacy shorthand such as `0.10.5` or `v0.10.5` may be accepted at boundaries, but must normalize through `normalizeRulesVersion()`.
- Schema versions are semantic versions, for example `2.2.0`, and normalize through `normalizeSchemaVersion()`.
- PDF versions are template identifiers, for example `0.10`; they are not the same as rules versions.
- System source metadata should point to a checked-in source artifact and named sections or line ranges when practical.

## 3. Ownership

| Concern                          | Source of truth                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Known/current rules versions     | `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/rulesVersion.ts`                                       |
| Character compatibility gates    | `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/compatibility.ts`                                      |
| Rules upgrade mappings           | `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/aliases.ts`                                            |
| Explicit character upgrade flow  | `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/characterUpgrade.ts`                                   |
| Storage schema version           | `src/lib/types/schemaVersion.ts`                                                     |
| Character storage shape          | `src/lib/types/dataContracts.ts`, `docs/systems/DATABASE_SYSTEM.MD`                  |
| PDF routing                      | `src/lib/rulesdata/versioning/compatibility.ts`, `docs/systems/PDF_EXPORT_SYSTEM.MD` |
| PDF field-version audits         | `scripts/pdf/auditPdfFields.mjs`, `scripts/pdf/pdfFieldAuditService.mjs`             |
| Equipage source/version metadata | `src/lib/rulesdata/equipment/schemas/baseEquipment.ts`                               |

Equipage also owns a separate localStorage envelope version. Version 2 adds the
`generalEquipment` array; version-1 data and imports remain valid and normalize a
missing array to empty. This does not change character `schemaVersion` or rules identity.

## 4. Rules Version Policy

`rulesVersion` is the rules interpretation fence.

- New characters are saved with `CURRENT_RULES_VERSION`.
- Missing `rulesVersion` means legacy `dc20-0.10`.
- A character whose `rulesVersion` is not current must not be silently recalculated under current rules.
- Compatibility is classified as:
  - `editable`: full render, edit, recalculation, auto-save.
  - `upgrade-required`: render/export allowed from stored values; build and sheet-content edits, level-up, and recalculation rewrites are blocked. Owners may change only existing HP, Temp HP, MP, SP, Rest, Grit, and Exhaustion values, which auto-save without recalculation.
  - `view-only`: best-effort render, no auto-save, no edit/level-up.
- Explicit upgrade must create a new current-rules draft and leave the original legacy character's build and sheet content locked. Its permitted live resource values remain independently mutable.
- Pure aliases, reworks, deprecated IDs, and ambiguous IDs must be represented in `RULES_ALIASES`. Despite the legacy constant name, this is the cross-system upgrade mapping catalog, not only a spell-alias table.

### 4.1 Character Rules Migration

Rules migration is a create-new-version flow, not an in-place edit.

Required behavior:

1. Load the legacy character with resource-only controls; all build and sheet-content controls remain read-only.
2. Build a migration plan from the upgrade mapping catalog before writing data.
3. Create a new current-rules draft record with a new ID and `rulesUpgradeSourceId` pointing at the locked source.
4. Preserve the source character's build and sheet content unchanged unless the user explicitly deletes it; live resource counters may continue to change.
5. Apply automatic aliases and approved reworks in the draft.
6. Recalculate all current-rules derived values that the calculator can determine from the migrated draft.
   - The draft must be stamped with `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
   - Recalculation must persist calculated display/export arrays such as resistances, vulnerabilities, senses, and combat training.
   - The draft must normalize partial legacy `characterState` before save so
     Convex can create the current-rules copy even when the source record has
     incomplete nested runtime resources.
   - The Convex save boundary must remove calculator-only, creation-input, and
     JSON export envelope fields carried through upgrade object spreads; these
     are not part of the persisted character schema.
7. Mark the draft as `rulesUpgradeStatus: "needs-review"` when retired/deprecated selections were removed or require player alternatives.
8. Force unresolved retired/ambiguous choices through explicit user selection before treating the upgrade as complete.

Migration UX must show the plan before creating the draft: automatic renames, reworks, retired selections, blockers, source rules version, target rules version, and the new draft identity.

`needs-review` drafts should send the user back through the normal character creation/editing flow with illegal retired choices unselected. The user resolves missing alternatives there, then saves the draft as the updated current-rules character.

If a legacy character already has a current-rules copy, the default action opens the existing copy. Creating another migrated copy must be an explicit secondary action.

`rulesUpgradeStatus: "needs-review"` applies to any risky migration result, including removed selections, reworked selections, unresolved validation, or failed recalculation.

## 5. Schema Version Policy

`schemaVersion` is only the saved-data shape version.

- It must not imply rules text, rules behavior, PDF template, or app release version.
- Backward-compatible saved-data additions bump minor or patch according to `schemaVersion.ts` guidance.
- Breaking saved-data changes require a major version and an explicit migration plan.
- Automatic schema migrations may fill missing fields or normalize legacy structures, but must not reinterpret old rules choices.

Campaign membership's optional `sharedCharacterDocIds` is an additive backend-table compatibility field, not a `SavedCharacter` shape change. Legacy app-ID links remain owner-scoped and readable; reconnect lazily records the exact character IDs. No character `schemaVersion` bump is required.

The optional canonical `customWeapon` snapshot inside an attack is also an additive
field within the already-permissive attack-array payload. It does not change the
character envelope or require a schema-version bump; attacks without the snapshot retain
their existing catalog/name-based behavior.

## 6. PDF Version Policy

PDF versioning follows available fillable templates and field maps.

- Rules versions route to PDF versions through `getPdfVersionForRulesVersion()`.
- `dc20-0.10.5` currently routes to the `0.10` PDF template because the supported v0.10.5 fillable export target is the same template/field map as v0.10.
- PDF export always reads stored `SavedCharacter` values and must not run current-rules recalculation during export.
- PDF export must not apply compatibility aliases or rules-upgrade decisions. It can format exact current catalog IDs for display, but legacy/reworked saved IDs remain the stored value.
- Unsupported or future rules versions may export on a best-effort basis when the routing layer can map them to an available template.
- Before adding or changing a supported PDF version, run the generic PDF field audit service against the previous and new templates. The service is version-agnostic; labels such as `0.10` or `0.10.5` are report metadata, not runtime routing rules.
- A PDF audit report may justify reusing an existing template/field map, adding a new versioned field map, or adding a new template route. Runtime export must still use explicit versioned helpers and maps.

## 7. System Source Metadata

When a subsystem is audited or updated against a rules release, record its source.

Minimum standard:

- Current rules version.
- Checked-in source artifact path.
- Relevant section names or line ranges.
- Runtime constant when that subsystem stores/export data independently.

Example:

```typescript
export const EQUIPMENT_RULES_SOURCE = {
	version: EQUIPMENT_RULES_VERSION,
	name: 'DC20 RPG 0.10.5 Beta v1',
	path: 'docs/assets/dc20-0.10.5/DC20 0.10.5 clean.md',
	sections: {
		weapons: 'Equipment > Weapon Properties / Creating Weapons'
	}
} as const;
```

System docs must mention the same source in a “Rules Source & Version” section when the system owns rules data.

## 8. Change Checklist

When changing rules data or behavior:

1. Identify the affected system docs before editing.
2. Confirm the source artifact and section.
3. Decide whether this is a schema change, rules change, PDF routing change, or app-only behavior change.
4. If rules identity changes, update `RULES_ALIASES`.
5. If old data should remain loadable but not editable, ensure compatibility gates classify it correctly.
6. If stored/exported subsystem data has its own `rulesVersion`, preserve it on import/export and stamp new saves.
7. If the change adds or changes a PDF template, run `npm run pdf:fields:audit -- --old <old-pdf> --new <new-pdf> --field-map <map.ts>` and commit the relevant report.
8. Add focused tests for normalization, compatibility, upgrade, or behavior as appropriate.
9. Update the relevant `docs/systems/*.MD` timestamp.

## 9. Anti-Patterns

- Do not use `package.json.version` to infer rules behavior.
- Do not use `schemaVersion` to infer rules behavior.
- Do not silently rewrite legacy saved choices without the explicit upgrade flow.
- Do not add a new rules release by editing scattered string literals; add constants and normalization first.
- Do not treat PDF version and rules version as identical unless the template and field map are actually version-aligned.
